# Nexus Complete Journey Universe

This is the authoritative master catalogue of end-to-end business journeys for Nexus, as the product exists today. It is a planning and cataloguing artifact only: no journey in this document has been executed, and nothing in the product was changed to produce it.

## Mission and scope

Nexus is treated as a real operating system used by Finance, Legal, Customer Success, Leadership, Operations, Admins, Makers, Checkers, Workflow Admins, and users with restricted or read-only access. Every journey below answers some version of: what can a person do, on what object, in what state, with what permission, while what else is changing or failing.

This catalogue is coverage-driven, not number-driven. It was built by grounding every journey in the actual current codebase and documentation (routes, domain types, RPCs, error tokens, migrations), not in assumptions about what Nexus should eventually do. Where a capability does not exist yet, it is marked as a PRODUCT GAP or moved into one of the two FUTURE packs at the end, never quietly treated as if it already worked.

## How to read a journey record

Every journey uses the same record shape:

Journey ID, Pack, Business Objective, Domain, Object / Record Type, Starting State, Personas, Preconditions, Regular Path, Stress Variant, Authorization Variant, Concurrency Variant, Idempotency Variant, Audit/Data Integrity Checks, Recovery/Resilience Variant, UX Checks, Historical Variant, Expected Business Result, Expected Technical Invariants, Priority, Automation Feasibility, Dependencies, Related Journeys, Notes.

A field reads "N/A" when that dimension genuinely does not apply to that journey, rather than inventing a variant that adds no real coverage.

Journey IDs use a pack-letter prefix and a three-digit number, for example `A-014` or `V-047`, numbered independently within each pack.

### Priority definitions

- **P0**: could corrupt approved business or financial truth, bypass authorization, silently lose data, produce a wrong approval, wrong customer, wrong commercial version, or wrong workflow route, or destroy historical truth.
- **P1**: a core business journey is broken, a request is orphaned, ownership is incorrect, recovery is broken, or there is a major audit gap.
- **P2**: an important edge case, usability issue, or resilience gap.
- **P3**: low-risk polish or an unusual boundary condition.

### Automation feasibility

- **FULL**: can be scripted end to end today.
- **PARTIAL**: needs some manual setup, verification, or judgment alongside automation.
- **MANUAL**: requires a human to execute and judge (for example, subjective UX comprehension checks).

## Pack index

Packs A through AB (including ACC, added during gap analysis) are the CURRENT, executable universe (783 journeys, including K-030, added during Batch 1 execution as a regression journey for a real defect found and fixed live). Packs FH and MRR are FUTURE, planned-only coverage for modules that do not exist in the product yet (44 high-level placeholder entries) and are explicitly excluded from the current executable count.

## A note on pack V

Pack V (Concurrency) deliberately also houses the "Permission-Change Journeys" and "State-Mutation Journeys" scenario families as its own labeled sub-sections, alongside pure concurrency races. All three are fundamentally the same shape of risk: something changes underneath live work while a person is mid-task. Splitting them into three separate top-level packs would have fragmented one coherent risk category; grouping them under Pack V keeps that coherence while still giving each family its own clearly labeled sub-section.

## A note on cross-cutting packs and duplication

Packs V, W, X, Y, and Z are engine-level and cross-domain by design. Where a race, retry, or failure scenario is mechanically identical across two or more of the four governed domains (Customer Onboarding, Customer Change, Commercial Configuration Version, Go Live) with no materially different terminal business mutation, it is written once, with every applicable domain listed in its Domain field, rather than duplicated per domain. Where the terminal mutation differs materially (for example, a double-approve on Go Live activates live billing, while a double-approve on Onboarding would double-create a Customer Master record), each domain gets its own dedicated journey. Domain packs (A through U) additionally carry their own Concurrency Variant, Idempotency Variant, and Authorization Variant fields inline on ordinary business journeys; Packs V/W/X/Y/Z hold the scenarios whose primary identity IS the cross-cutting mechanism itself, not a variant of a business journey that belongs to one domain.

## Pack A: Customer Onboarding

### A-001: Create draft onboarding case
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Maker can start a new onboarding case and save initial customer details without committing to submission.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (status: draft)
- Starting State: No case exists for this prospective customer.
- Personas: Maker (onboarding creator)
- Preconditions: Maker holds customer.create permission.
- Regular Path: Maker calls createOnboardingCaseAction with initial customer_details stage data; case is created in draft status with created_by set to maker; case is retrievable and editable.
- Stress Variant: Create with minimal required fields only, verify no premature validation of later stages.
- Authorization Variant: User without customer.create permission attempts creation, expect denial.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: Double-submit of the create form (double click) should not create two cases; verify a single case record results.
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: created_by/created_at populated correctly; case_number or key generated uniquely.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Draft appears in maker's "My Cases" list immediately with correct status label.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: A draft case exists, editable only by creator, not yet visible to reviewers.
- Expected Technical Invariants: status = draft; created_by = actor_user_id; no workflow node yet advanced.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: A-002, A-003
- Notes: N/A

### A-002: Save draft across multiple stages incrementally
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Maker can save partial progress across the five stages without losing data between sessions.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (status: draft)
- Starting State: Draft case exists with customer_details stage partially filled.
- Personas: Maker
- Preconditions: Case in draft status, owned by maker.
- Regular Path: Maker calls saveOnboardingDraftAction repeatedly across sessions, filling tax_registration, then commercial_documents, then commercial_rate; each save persists only the stage payload sent; case remains in draft.
- Stress Variant: Save with a very large customer_fields payload (all 25 governed fields populated) in one call.
- Authorization Variant: Another user (non-creator, non-admin) attempts to save the draft, expect denial.
- Concurrency Variant: Two browser tabs open the same draft; second save is rejected with `ONBOARDING_DRAFT_STALE` if the draft changed underneath it (see A-030 for the dedicated concurrency regression journey).
- Idempotency Variant: Saving identical stage data twice in a row produces no unintended side effects (no duplicate documents, no duplicate history).
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Each stage's data is persisted independently; earlier stage data is not clobbered by later stage saves.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Browser refresh mid-edit reloads last saved state, not in-memory unsaved state.
- UX Checks: Stage completion indicators update as each stage becomes complete.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Maker can build up a complete case over multiple sessions without data loss.
- Expected Technical Invariants: status remains draft throughout; `workflow_version_id` was already resolved and stamped once at case creation (A-001) if an active published workflow existed at that time, and stays constant across every draft save in this journey; it is never re-resolved mid-draft.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: A-001
- Related Journeys: A-003, A-030
- Notes: N/A

### A-003: First submit with all validated stages complete
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Maker submits a fully-prepared case for reviewer approval.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (draft -> submitted)
- Starting State: Draft case with customer_details, tax_registration, commercial_documents, commercial_rate stages complete; agreement_approval intentionally incomplete (by design, excluded from validation).
- Personas: Maker
- Preconditions: No hard duplicate blockers (GST/PAN unique); workflow, if any, resolved at case creation.
- Regular Path: Maker calls submitOnboardingCaseAction; server validates first four stages strictly, runs duplicate detection, resolves workflow node (or default approval mechanism), transitions status to submitted.
- Stress Variant: Submit with all 25 governed customer_fields populated plus maximum documents attached.
- Authorization Variant: N/A (submit is maker's own action, but confirm only the creator or an assigned collaborator can submit, per product's actual model, verify against code).
- Concurrency Variant: N/A (see A-030 for stale draft concurrency)
- Idempotency Variant: Attempting to submit an already-submitted case is rejected with ONBOARDING_CASE_NOT_SUBMITTABLE (see A-015).
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Submission timestamp and actor recorded; case now visible in reviewer queue.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Success confirmation; case now read-only for maker except via send-back cycle.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Case enters reviewer workflow.
- Expected Technical Invariants: status = submitted; agreement_approval stage completeness never gates this transition.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: A-001, A-002
- Related Journeys: A-004, A-026
- Notes: N/A

### A-004: Submit blocked by incomplete required stage
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Prevent submission of cases missing required data in the strictly-validated stages.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (draft)
- Starting State: Draft case missing a required field in tax_registration stage (e.g. no tax_registration_number).
- Personas: Maker
- Preconditions: Case in draft.
- Regular Path: Maker attempts submitOnboardingCaseAction; server-side stage validation fails; case remains in draft with field-level error surfaced.
- Stress Variant: Multiple missing fields across multiple stages simultaneously, verify all are surfaced, not just the first.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No status change persisted; no partial submission side effects (no duplicate check run, no workflow node advanced).
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Maker can fix and resubmit without losing other stage data.
- UX Checks: Clear per-field, per-stage error messaging directing maker to the incomplete stage.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Incomplete cases cannot enter reviewer queue.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Client AND server both enforce validation (server is source of truth even if client is bypassed).
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: A-001
- Related Journeys: A-003, A-026
- Notes: N/A

### A-005: Duplicate GST number hard blocker at submit
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Prevent onboarding of a customer with a GST number that exactly matches an existing customer, avoiding duplicate legal entities.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case
- Starting State: An existing customer (from a prior approved onboarding) has GST number X. A new draft case is entered with the same GST number X.
- Personas: Maker
- Preconditions: Existing customer with GST X exists in customers table.
- Regular Path: Maker attempts submitOnboardingCaseAction; server duplicate detection finds exact GST match; submission is hard-blocked with an explanatory error; case remains in draft.
- Stress Variant: GST entered with different casing/whitespace, verify exact-match normalization behavior (verify against code for normalization rules).
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: Two draft cases created concurrently with the same GST, both attempt submit; only detection at submit time matters, first submitter proceeds (subject to other checks), second is blocked once the first is approved and a real customer row exists, but if both submit before either is approved, verify actual duplicate-check timing (against draft cases vs. against real customers table only, per grounding: duplicate detection is at Submit only, verify scope against code).
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No new customer row created; case stays in draft, not silently advanced.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Maker can correct the GST or escalate for manual review.
- UX Checks: Error clearly identifies this as a hard blocker (not a warning), distinct visual treatment from soft warnings.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Duplicate legal entities by GST cannot enter the system.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Hard blockers prevent status transition entirely, unlike soft warnings.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: A-003 (requires an existing approved customer as the duplicate target)
- Related Journeys: A-006, A-007, A-008
- Notes: N/A

### A-009: Reviewer sends back case with per-field comments
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Reviewer requests corrections on specific fields without approving or fully rejecting the case (no reject state exists for onboarding).
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (submitted -> sent_back)
- Starting State: Case in submitted status.
- Personas: Reviewer/Checker (customer.approve holder)
- Preconditions: Reviewer is not the case creator.
- Regular Path: Reviewer calls sendBackOnboardingCaseAction with comments attached to specific fields (e.g. tax_registration_number); case transitions to sent_back; maker is notified.
- Stress Variant: Comments on fields across multiple stages simultaneously.
- Authorization Variant: Reviewer without customer.approve permission attempts send-back, expect denial.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Per-field comments are stored and retrievable against the specific case revision that was reviewed (ties to A-025 revision snapshot).
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Maker sees exactly which fields were flagged and why upon reopening the case.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Maker gets actionable, field-specific feedback rather than a generic rejection.
- Expected Technical Invariants: status = sent_back; no customer/commercial rows created; case remains editable only by maker next.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: A-003
- Related Journeys: A-010, A-025
- Notes: N/A

### A-010: Maker resubmits after send-back
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Maker corrects flagged fields and resubmits the case for another review pass.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (sent_back -> resubmitted)
- Starting State: Case in sent_back status with per-field comments.
- Personas: Maker
- Preconditions: Case is in sent_back status, owned by maker.
- Regular Path: Maker edits flagged fields (and possibly others), calls submitOnboardingCaseAction again (same action handles resubmit); server re-validates and re-runs duplicate detection; status transitions to resubmitted.
- Stress Variant: Maker changes GST/PAN during resubmission fix, triggering a fresh duplicate check that could newly hard-block.
- Authorization Variant: A different maker (not original creator, e.g. delegate) attempts resubmit, verify actual permission model (verify against code).
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: Resubmitting without changing anything still transitions status and re-validates.
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Previous reviewer comments are preserved historically even after resubmission (not overwritten).
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Reviewer sees this is a resubmission with prior comments visible alongside the changes made.
- Historical Variant: Multiple send-back/resubmit cycles on the same case, verify comment history across all cycles remains intact and distinguishable by cycle.
- Expected Business Result: Iterative correction cycle works without data loss across cycles.
- Expected Technical Invariants: status = resubmitted; workflow node resets to reviewer appropriately for another decision.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: A-009
- Related Journeys: A-009, A-025
- Notes: N/A

### A-011: Reviewer approves case, atomic Customer Master + Commercial Configuration + Version 1 creation
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Approval is the single moment a real customer legally exists in the system, together with its first commercial configuration.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding, Customer Master, Commercial (see Pack D/E for Commercial internals)
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (submitted/resubmitted -> approved), customers (new row), commercial_configuration (new), commercial_configuration_version (v1)
- Starting State: Case in submitted or resubmitted status, no duplicate hard blockers, reviewer is not the creator.
- Personas: Reviewer/Checker
- Preconditions: Reviewer holds customer.approve; case not already approved.
- Regular Path: Reviewer calls approveOnboardingCaseAction -> approve_customer_onboarding_case RPC; in one atomic transaction: customers row created from the 25 governed customer_fields, a Commercial Configuration is created via create_system_commercial_request/create_commercial_configuration_with_change, components added via add_commercial_component, commitments via add_commercial_commitment; case transitions to approved.
- Stress Variant: Approval with maximum commercial components attached in the commercial_rate stage.
- Authorization Variant: Reviewer without customer.approve attempts approval, expect denial; case creator attempts self-approval, expect SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED (see A-012 for dedicated coverage).
- Concurrency Variant: See A-031 for simultaneous approval race.
- Idempotency Variant: See A-032 for re-approval no-op.
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Every field written to customers exactly matches the case's final customer_fields snapshot at approval time; commercial configuration key/name match what was entered in commercial_rate stage; if any step in the transaction fails, NOTHING persists (all-or-nothing atomicity), verify no orphaned customers row without a commercial configuration, and vice versa.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Simulated failure mid-transaction (e.g. add_commercial_commitment failing) must roll back the entire transaction, leaving case in its pre-approval status, not a corrupted partial-approved state.
- UX Checks: Post-approval, maker and reviewer both see case as approved with a link to the newly created customer record.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: A single Approve action produces a fully-formed, commercially-configured customer, this is the true system of record moment.
- Expected Technical Invariants: This is the ONLY path (besides create_next_revision-driven flows) by which a customers row and its first commercial configuration are created; atomicity is non-negotiable.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL (atomicity/rollback testing may need direct DB-level fault injection)
- Dependencies: A-003 or A-010
- Related Journeys: A-012, A-013, A-014, A-032, AA-001
- Notes: N/A

### A-012: Self-approval blocked
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Prevent a maker from approving their own onboarding case, a fundamental segregation-of-duties control.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (submitted)
- Starting State: Case in submitted status, created by user U, U also happens to hold customer.approve permission.
- Personas: Maker/Checker (same person, dual-permission user)
- Preconditions: Actor U is both created_by and has approve permission.
- Regular Path: U attempts approveOnboardingCaseAction on their own case; server compares actor_user_id to created_by and rejects with SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED regardless of permission holding.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: This IS the authorization variant; core assertion is that permission alone is insufficient, identity check is separate and always enforced.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: Repeated self-approval attempts all fail identically.
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No customer/commercial rows created; failed attempt is logged in audit trail.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Clear error message distinguishing this from a generic permission error.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Segregation of duties is enforced even against a technically-permitted user.
- Expected Technical Invariants: This check is server-side and cannot be bypassed by client manipulation.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: A-003
- Related Journeys: A-011
- Notes: N/A

### A-013: Case creation blocked with no active workflow bound (RECONCILED 2026-09-20, superseded premise)
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Was originally "onboarding must remain approvable even when no Workflow Builder graph is configured." Migration `20260930000000_workflow_creation_requires_active_definition.sql` (applied before this journey's Batch 7 re-execution) made an active, published workflow mandatory for customer_onboarding case creation itself, raising `WORKFLOW_NO_ACTIVE_DEFINITION` otherwise. A case with `workflow_version_id = null` can therefore no longer be created at all, so the original "workflow-less approval" path this journey described is unreachable. Recorded here as history, not deleted, per this program's own no-renumbering/no-silent-rewrite rule.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case
- Starting State (current, re-verified live in Batch 7): No workflow version with applies_to = 'customer_onboarding' is both active and published.
- Personas: Maker
- Preconditions: None (this is now a creation-time invariant, not an approval-time one).
- Regular Path (current): Maker attempts to create a case; `create_customer_onboarding_case` raises `WORKFLOW_NO_ACTIVE_DEFINITION` before any row is written; case creation fails outright. There is no longer a "default approval mechanism" path to reach, since a case in this state cannot exist.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: N/A (superseded; the original variant about any customer.approve holder approving a workflow-less case cannot be exercised since such a case cannot be created)
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No `customer_onboarding_cases` row is written on a blocked creation attempt (confirmed live, Batch 7).
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result (current): Onboarding cannot begin at all while no workflow is configured for the domain; business continuity now depends on always keeping one workflow active, not on a workflow-less fallback.
- Expected Technical Invariants (current): `create_customer_onboarding_case` raises `WORKFLOW_NO_ACTIVE_DEFINITION` whenever no row in `workflow_definition_versions` joined to an active `workflow_definitions` row with `applies_to = 'customer_onboarding'` and `status = 'published'` exists.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: A-014, A-027
- Notes: Re-executed against current behavior during Batch 7 (see `docs/journey-runs/BATCH_07_RESULTS.md`). Final Status recorded there as EXPECTED BEHAVIOR CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY: the journey's original premise is stale (Category B, not a product defect), and current behavior (creation-time hard block) is itself the correct, intentional invariant. If a genuine workflow-less-approval fallback is ever wanted as a product decision, it would need a new journey ID, not a reopening of this one.

### A-014: Workflow version resolved once at creation, unaffected by later publishes
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Guarantee that an in-flight onboarding case follows a stable, predictable approval path even if the organization publishes a new workflow version while the case is in progress.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case
- Starting State: Workflow version W1 (applies_to = 'customer_onboarding') is the sole active+published version at the time case C is created; W1 is bound to C.
- Personas: Maker, Workflow Admin, Reviewer
- Preconditions: A workflow admin publishes a new version W2 (making it active+published, possibly deactivating W1) after C is created but before C is approved.
- Regular Path: Case C continues to route according to W1's graph and team assignments, completely unaffected by W2's existence or activation; case C is approved following W1's rules.
- Stress Variant: W2 is published, then a THIRD version W3 is published, all while C is still in flight; C remains bound to W1 throughout.
- Authorization Variant: If W1 designated Team A and W2 designates Team B for the equivalent node, only Team A members can act on case C's node (never Team B), verify this precisely.
- Concurrency Variant: Workflow publish happens concurrently with a reviewer action on case C, verify no race causes C to suddenly reference W2.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Case C's stored workflow_version_id never changes after creation; audit trail shows W1 throughout C's lifecycle.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Reviewer UI for case C shows W1-based routing information, not W2, even if W2 is now the "current" workflow shown elsewhere in the product.
- Historical Variant: A case created back when W1 was active, later reviewed long after W3 is active, must still resolve against W1 at every step.
- Expected Business Result: In-flight cases are never silently re-routed by administrative changes to workflow configuration.
- Expected Technical Invariants: workflow_version_id is set once at create_customer_onboarding_case and never re-resolved.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: A-001
- Related Journeys: A-013, AA-016
- Notes: N/A

### A-027: Workflow node with zero active team members blocks approval indefinitely
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Surface the real, currently unhandled risk that a case can become permanently stuck if the responsible team for its current workflow node has no active members.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding

- Starting State: Case is submitted and routed to workflow node N, whose responsible_team_id has zero currently-active (non-revoked) members (e.g. all were offboarded after the graph was configured).

- Preconditions: Team membership for the node's team has been fully revoked or was never populated.
- Regular Path: Any user attempts to approve/send-back the case; server raises WORKFLOW_TEAM_REQUIRED; case remains stuck in submitted/resubmitted status with no built-in recovery mechanism.
- Stress Variant: N/A

- Idempotency Variant: Repeated attempts all fail identically, no automatic retry or alternate routing occurs.
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Failed attempts should still be visible for support/ops triage (verify whether these are logged distinctly).
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: This journey IS the recovery-gap journey: document that resolution today requires an admin to manually fix team membership or the workflow graph outside the normal user flow; there is no automated recovery.
- UX Checks: The error message shown to the approver should clearly indicate a team-configuration problem, not a generic failure, to enable faster support escalation.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Currently a known gap: business impact is a stuck case with no self-service recovery.
- Expected Technical Invariants: WORKFLOW_TEAM_REQUIRED is raised deterministically every time this condition holds.

- Automation Feasibility: FULL

### A-029: Stale page approve attempt surfaces friendly WORKFLOW_NODE_ALREADY_ADVANCED

- Authorization Variant: N/A

- Idempotency Variant: N/A

- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Reviewer A refreshes and sees the case's true current state (already advanced by B), no corruption occurs.

- Priority: P1

- Notes: N/A

### A-030: Concurrent two-tab draft save is rejected with a staleness error, not silently overwritten (regression)
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Prove that two open tabs editing the same onboarding draft can no longer silently clobber each other, since `save_customer_onboarding_draft` now takes `p_expected_row_version` and rejects a stale write with `ONBOARDING_DRAFT_STALE` (migration `20260922000000_optimistic_locking_extension.sql`, confirmed applied in the live migration ledger). This is now a regression journey guarding a fixed defect, not an open-gap verification.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (draft), submission_revisions
- Starting State: Maker opens the same draft case in two browser tabs (Tab 1 and Tab 2), both loaded with the same `submission_revisions.row_version`.
- Personas: Maker (single user, two tabs; or two collaborating makers with edit access)
- Preconditions: Draft case exists and is editable.
- Regular Path: Tab 1 edits field X and saves; the save succeeds and `submission_revisions.row_version` increments. Tab 2, still holding the pre-edit `row_version`, edits field Y and attempts to save with its now-stale `p_expected_row_version`; confirm the call is rejected with `ONBOARDING_DRAFT_STALE` rather than silently overwriting Tab 1's change.
- Stress Variant: Rapid alternating saves from both tabs in quick succession; confirm every stale attempt is rejected, never just the first one.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This IS the concurrency journey.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm Tab 1's change to field X survives untouched in the database after Tab 2's rejected save; confirm `row_version` incremented exactly once, from Tab 1's successful save only.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Tab 2's user reloads to pick up the current `row_version` and content, reapplies field Y, and saves successfully; confirm no data is silently lost across this reload-and-reapply cycle.
- UX Checks: Tab 2 sees the actionable "This draft was changed by someone else since you loaded it. Refresh the page to see the latest version before saving your changes." message, not a silent success and not a raw SQL/RPC error.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: No silent data loss for concurrent onboarding draft edits; the loser is told clearly and can recover cleanly.
- Expected Technical Invariants: `save_customer_onboarding_draft` compares the caller's `p_expected_row_version` against the current `submission_revisions.row_version` under a row lock and raises `ONBOARDING_DRAFT_STALE` on mismatch, mirroring `save_customer_change_draft` exactly.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL (requires orchestrating true concurrent tab state, best done as a scripted two-session test)
- Dependencies: A-001, A-002
- Related Journeys: AA-014, V-012
- Notes: Reconciled 2026-09-16: this was previously catalogued as a known, unfixed gap. The optimistic-locking migration is confirmed applied via the live Supabase migration ledger (version `20260922000000`), not merely written to a file. Downgraded from P0 to P1 accordingly, since the underlying risk (silent draft data loss) is now closed and this journey exists to guard the fix, not to document an open exposure.

- Starting State: Case in submitted status, two distinct eligible reviewers (both non-creator, both customer.approve holders, both eligible for the current node's team) simultaneously attempt to approve.
- Personas: Reviewer A, Reviewer B
- Preconditions: Both A and B load the case while it is still submitted.
- Regular Path: Both submit approveOnboardingCaseAction near-simultaneously; the RPC's SELECT...FOR UPDATE row lock serializes the two attempts; the first to acquire the lock proceeds through the full atomic creation (A-011); the second, upon acquiring the lock afterward, finds the case no longer approvable and receives ONBOARDING_CASE_NOT_APPROVABLE (or the friendlier WORKFLOW_NODE_ALREADY_ADVANCED if expected_current_node_key was supplied).
- Stress Variant: Extend to three or more simultaneous reviewers for the same node.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This IS the concurrency journey.
- Idempotency Variant: Exactly one customers row and one commercial configuration are created, never two.
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Verify at the database level that no duplicate customers row exists for this case; verify the audit trail shows exactly one approval event as authoritative and one rejected/failed attempt.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: The losing reviewer's UI should refresh to reflect the true approved state gracefully.
- UX Checks: Losing reviewer sees a clear "already approved by [other reviewer]" state, not a raw error.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: No duplicate customer/commercial creation under concurrent approval attempts, this is a P0 correctness guarantee.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Row lock (SELECT...FOR UPDATE) plus status guard is the true correctness mechanism, independent of any client-supplied hints.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL (requires true concurrent request orchestration, e.g. two near-simultaneous server calls)
- Dependencies: A-003
- Related Journeys: A-011, A-017, A-029
- Notes: N/A

### A-032: Idempotent re-approval of an already-approved case is a no-op
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: A retried or duplicated approval network call must never create a second customer/commercial configuration for the same case.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding, Customer Master, Commercial
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (approved), customers, commercial_configuration
- Starting State: Case already approved (customers row and commercial configuration v1 already exist and linked).
- Personas: Reviewer (via network retry, double-click, or replayed request)
- Preconditions: Case status is already approved.
- Regular Path: approve_customer_onboarding_case is invoked again against this case (e.g. due to a client-side retry after a timeout that actually succeeded server-side); the RPC detects the case is already approved and returns the existing linkage (existing customer id, existing commercial configuration id) without creating anything new.
- Stress Variant: Multiple rapid repeated calls (5+) against the same already-approved case.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: This IS the idempotency journey.
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm at the database level that only one customers row and one commercial configuration/version exist for this case no matter how many times re-approval is attempted; confirm no duplicate audit log entries misrepresent multiple approval events.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: This idempotency is itself the resilience mechanism protecting against network retry duplication.
- UX Checks: Repeated approval attempt (e.g. accidental double-click) should feel like a harmless no-op to the user, not an error and not a duplicate side effect.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Safe against retries and double-submits, a core financial-integrity guarantee.
- Expected Technical Invariants: approve_customer_onboarding_case is explicitly idempotent on the approved state per the grounding brief.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: A-011
- Related Journeys: A-031
- Notes: N/A

### A-036: Viewing another maker's draft onboarding case by request_id (new, discovered Batch 7)
- Pack: A - Customer Onboarding
- Business Objective: Confirm the intended visibility model for an in-progress (draft/sent_back) onboarding case: should any holder of customer.create be able to open and read a case they did not create, purely by knowing or guessing its request_id?
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (draft/sent_back), submission_revisions
- Starting State: User A creates a draft case. User B, a different maker holding only customer.create (not the creator, not a reviewer), attempts to read A's case by its request_id.
- Personas: Maker A (creator), Maker B (non-creator, same broad permission)
- Preconditions: Both users hold customer.create; neither is a reviewer for this case.
- Regular Path (current, confirmed live during Batch 7): the onboarding case detail read path authorizes on the blanket `customer.create` permission only, with no check that the caller is the case's own creator. Maker B's read succeeds and returns Maker A's full draft (all customer/tax fields, comments, documents). Architectural detail withheld here per this program's own "not a security exploit manual" rule; the specific route and reproduction steps are not recorded in the Universe or ledger while this gap remains unfixed.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: This IS the authorization variant; mutation (Save, Submit) is now creator-only as of Batch 7's fix (migration `20260930050000_onboarding_draft_save_submit_creator_only.sql`, discovered while executing A-002/A-003's own authorization variants), but read access was deliberately left unchanged pending this journey's own product decision.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No mutation occurs on a read-only view, so nothing is written; the concern is confidentiality of in-progress business data (customer legal name, tax IDs, contact details), not integrity.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Undecided; depends on whether same-team visibility into in-progress drafts is an intended collaboration feature or an oversight.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Undecided pending product decision; if creator-only read is chosen, `getOnboardingCase`'s caller (the page route) would need a `created_by` check equivalent to what Save/Submit now enforce.
- Priority: P2 (read-only exposure of pre-submission business data to other holders of the same broad permission, not a mutation risk)
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: A-001, A-002
- Related Journeys: A-002, A-003, A-019
- Notes: Discovered during Batch 7 while investigating A-002/A-003's authorization variants (see `docs/journey-runs/BATCH_07_RESULTS.md`, DEFECT-B7-002). Classified as Category F (genuine gap needing a product decision, not a bounded fix): unlike Save/Submit, there is no existing precedent in this codebase for whether onboarding draft reads should be creator-scoped, and narrowing it could break an undocumented legitimate collaboration path if one exists. Scheduled for a future batch's authorization sweep, not fixed in Batch 7.

- Historical Variant: N/A

- Pack: C - Customer Change
- Business Objective: Prevent approving a change request against a customer whose real row has been modified by something else since the request was created, which would otherwise silently overwrite or misapply changes to a moved target.
- Domain: Customer Change, Customer Master
- Object / Record Type: customer_change_request, customers
- Starting State: Change request R created against customer C at customers.rowVersion = N (captured as base_customer_row_version). Before R is approved, a SEPARATE approved action (e.g. another change request, R2, approved first) advances customers.rowVersion to N+1.
- Personas: Maker (creator of R), Reviewer (attempting to approve R), Maker/Reviewer of the intervening R2
- Preconditions: A second governed action on the same customer completes and advances rowVersion between R's creation and R's approval.
- Regular Path: Reviewer attempts approveChangeRequestAction on R; approve_customer_change_request RE-VERIFIES customers.row_version against R's captured base_customer_row_version, finds a mismatch (N+1 != N), and raises CUSTOMER_CHANGE_STALE_BASE; R is NOT approved; no fields are written.
- Stress Variant: Multiple intervening changes (rowVersion advances by 3+ before R's approval is attempted).
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This is fundamentally a concurrency/staleness journey, and is DISTINCT from C-004's draft-level guard, per the grounding brief's explicit callout that these are two separate protections.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm this check re-verifies at APPROVAL time (not merely at submit time), since the customer row could change even after R is already submitted and awaiting review.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: The reviewer/maker must re-review R's proposed changes against the customer's now-current state (potentially re-creating or amending R) before it can be approved; document the actual recommended recovery path (verify against code/UX for what options are offered here).
- UX Checks: Clear messaging distinguishing this staleness error from a generic failure, ideally showing what changed on the customer in the interim.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Prevents a genuinely dangerous class of bug: approving stale proposed changes against a customer record that has since moved on, which could silently corrupt or misapply business data.
- Expected Technical Invariants: This check is enforced at approval time inside approve_customer_change_request itself, independent of and in addition to the draft-level guard in C-004.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL (requires orchestrating two concurrent/sequential governed actions against the same customer)
- Dependencies: C-001, C-005
- Related Journeys: C-004, C-029, AA-006
- Notes: N/A

### C-007: Segment change triggers FINANCE_HEAD informational requirement
- Pack: C - Customer Change
- Business Objective: Surface finance leadership context whenever a customer's segment is being changed, per the static CUSTOMER_CHANGE_WORKFLOW_RULES ruleset.

- Object / Record Type: customer_change_request, customer_change_request_requirements
- Starting State: Draft request proposing a segment change (e.g. SMB -> Enterprise).
- Personas: Maker, Reviewer
- Preconditions: proposedValues includes segment.
- Regular Path: At submit, CUSTOMER_CHANGE_WORKFLOW_RULES computes a FINANCE_HEAD context requirement; it is persisted to customer_change_request_requirements and displayed to the reviewer, but does NOT create a separate sign-off gate, a single Approve/Send Back/Reject by any customer.approve holder still governs the whole request.
- Stress Variant: Segment change combined with several other unrelated field changes in the same request.
- Authorization Variant: A reviewer with NO particular finance-head role can still approve the whole request unilaterally, confirming this is informational/transparency-only in V1, not an enforced gate.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: The requirement record persists and remains visible/retrievable after approval, for historical transparency of what context existed at decision time.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Requirement is clearly displayed to the reviewer as informational context, not as a blocking checklist item.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Reviewers get relevant business context without an over-engineered multi-sign-off gate (a deliberate V1 simplification).
- Expected Technical Invariants: Requirements are computed and persisted at submit; they never alter the single-approver authorization model.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: C-005
- Related Journeys: C-008, C-009, C-010, C-011
- Notes: N/A

### C-014: Reject is terminal and never touches the customers table
- Pack: C - Customer Change

- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: A genuine terminal negative decision exists in this domain, unlike onboarding.

### C-017: Approve happy path writes field history per actually-changed field
- Pack: C - Customer Change
- Business Objective: Approving a change request applies proposed values to the real customer record and creates a precise, field-scoped audit trail.
- Domain: Customer Change, Customer Master
- Object / Record Type: customer_change_request (-> approved), customers, customer_field_history
- Starting State: Submitted/resubmitted request proposing changes to three fields, all three genuinely differing from current customer values; base_customer_row_version still matches current customers.rowVersion.
- Personas: Reviewer
- Preconditions: Reviewer is not the request creator; no staleness (C-006 does not fire).
- Regular Path: Reviewer calls approveChangeRequestAction; approve_customer_change_request re-verifies row_version, applies all three field changes to customers, writes exactly three customer_field_history rows (one per actually-changed field), transitions request to approved.
- Stress Variant: Maximum realistic number of fields changed in one request.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: See C-006, C-029.
- Idempotency Variant: See C-020.
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Exactly one history row per actually-changed field, each recording old value, new value, actor, and timestamp; customers row reflects the new values exactly; rowVersion increments.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Post-approval, customer detail page reflects new values immediately; Activity/former-name history (B-007) picks up any name change.
- Historical Variant: This journey feeds directly into B-007's former-name search and B-014's deletion-ineligibility check.
- Expected Business Result: The sole path (alongside onboarding approval) by which customer master fields legitimately change after initial creation.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Field history is append-only and field-scoped; only genuinely changed fields get a row.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: C-005
- Related Journeys: C-018, C-006, B-007, B-014, B-021
- Notes: N/A

- Idempotency Variant: N/A

### C-029: Two concurrent change requests on the same customer, first-approved wins
- Pack: C - Customer Change
- Business Objective: Confirm correct behavior when two independent change requests are both drafted/submitted against the same customer before either is approved.
- Domain: Customer Change, Customer Master
- Object / Record Type: customer_change_request (two instances, R1 and R2), customers
- Starting State: R1 and R2 both created against customer C at the same base_customer_row_version = N, both later submitted.
- Personas: Maker 1 (creator of R1), Maker 2 (creator of R2), Reviewer(s)
- Preconditions: Neither has been approved yet.
- Regular Path: Reviewer approves R1 first; customers.rowVersion advances to N+1; reviewer then attempts to approve R2, whose base_customer_row_version is still N; CUSTOMER_CHANGE_STALE_BASE fires (per C-006's mechanism), forcing R2 to be re-evaluated/recreated against the now-current customer state rather than blindly applied.
- Stress Variant: R1 and R2 propose overlapping fields (both touch billing_currency with different values) versus disjoint fields (no overlap), verify the staleness guard fires uniformly regardless of overlap, since it is a whole-row version check, not a field-level check.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This IS the concurrency journey; it is the natural real-world scenario that C-006's mechanism exists to protect against.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm R2's proposed values are never silently applied on top of R1's already-approved changes without a fresh staleness check; whole-row version granularity means even disjoint-field requests still collide.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Reviewer/maker must handle R2 via resubmission against the new base state; document actual recommended process (verify against code/product for whether R2 auto-recreates its base_customer_row_version on resubmit, or must be entirely recreated).
- UX Checks: Clear guidance to the user handling R2 about why it can no longer be approved as-is.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: No customer record ever has a change blindly applied against outdated assumptions about its state, even under legitimate multi-request concurrency.
- Expected Technical Invariants: base_customer_row_version staleness check is whole-row, not field-level; this is a deliberate simplicity/safety tradeoff.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: C-006
- Related Journeys: C-006, AA-006
- Notes: N/A

- Pack: C - Customer Change

- Authorization Variant: N/A

## Pack D: Commercial Configuration

### D-001: Create first Commercial Configuration identity via Onboarding approval
- Pack: D - Commercial Configuration
- Business Objective: Confirm a new customer's commercial relationship identity is minted correctly on onboarding approval.
- Domain: Commercial Configuration, Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: commercial_configurations, commercial_changes (initial_setup)
- Starting State: Customer Onboarding case in draft with a proposed commercial section, no commercial_configurations row yet.
- Personas: Onboarding Analyst (creator), Approver (finance manager)
- Preconditions: Onboarding case reaches the approval step with a valid unique key candidate for the configuration.
- Regular Path: Analyst completes onboarding case with commercial terms; Approver approves; create_commercial_configuration_with_change fires atomically, inserting commercial_configurations row plus its first commercial_changes row (change_category = initial_setup) and initial components.
- Stress Variant: Onboarding case with a very long relationship_note (near column limit) and multiple components in the initial set.
- Authorization Variant: Approver attempting to approve their own submitted onboarding case is blocked (SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED).
- Concurrency Variant: Two approvers open the same onboarding case approval screen simultaneously; second approval attempt after first succeeds must no-op or fail cleanly, not double-create the configuration.
- Idempotency Variant: Retry of the approval RPC call after a network timeout (client resubmits) must not create a duplicate commercial_configurations row or duplicate initial commercial_changes row.
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: commercial_configurations.key is unique; commercial_changes row exists with change_category = initial_setup and is the sole change at this point; components reference this change_id.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Approval RPC fails mid-transaction (simulated DB error) - verify no partial configuration or orphaned components row exists (all-or-nothing).
- UX Checks: Post-approval, Commercial Configuration detail view shows Version 1 derived purely from this single change, no separate version record to browse.
- Historical Variant: N/A (this is the origin point).
- Expected Business Result: Exactly one active Commercial Configuration identity exists for the customer with a coherent first set of components effective from the onboarding go-live date.
- Expected Technical Invariants: is_active starts true; key is globally unique; commercial_change_id chain starts clean; no commercial_configuration_versions row was created for this initial path.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: Customer Onboarding case approval workflow
- Related Journeys: E-001, E-002
- Notes: Initial setup deliberately bypasses the draft/submit/review cycle used for later changes.

### D-008: Component removed in latest version is surfaced as "removed" in diff, not deleted
- Pack: D - Commercial Configuration
- Business Objective: Confirm that a component absent from a newly approved version is never physically deleted, only closed, and the diff correctly labels it "removed" rather than silently vanishing from history.
- Domain: Commercial Configuration
- Object / Record Type: commercial_components, CommercialRateDiff
- Starting State: Active version has Component A and Component B; a new Commercial Change is approved carrying only Component A (B intentionally dropped).
- Personas: Finance Manager (approver), Auditor (viewer)
- Preconditions: Approval RPC executes its unconditional-closure step.
- Regular Path: After approval, Component B's row has effective_to set (closed) with no successor; CommercialRateDiff shows B with status "removed"; A shows "unchanged" or "changed" depending on whether its terms differ.
- Stress Variant: All components dropped in the new version except one, to confirm the closure loop handles bulk removal correctly.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Component B's historical row is still queryable by id; it is never hard-deleted; its stable_component_key does not reappear on any later open component unless explicitly re-added by a user action.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Diff view visually distinguishes "removed" from "changed" so an approver reviewing the version does not miss a dropped commercial term.
- Historical Variant: Querying "as of" a date within B's old effective range still returns B's terms correctly.
- Expected Business Result: No historical financial commitment is ever silently erased; removals are explicit and auditable.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Unconditional closure step in approve_commercial_configuration_version behaves identically whether a component is carried forward or dropped; only presence in the submitted list determines recreation.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: E-006

### D-010: FX snapshot rate remains frozen after Reference Master rate changes later
- Pack: D - Commercial Configuration
- Business Objective: Confirm a component's fx_snapshot_rate, captured at creation, is never recomputed even when the Reference Master currency rate is updated afterward.
- Domain: Commercial Configuration
- Object / Record Type: commercial_components
- Starting State: Component created in USD with fx_snapshot_rate = 83.00 (INR) at creation time.
- Personas: Finance Manager, FX/Treasury admin (updates Reference Master rate)
- Preconditions: Reference Master INR/USD rate is later changed to 85.00 for new records.
- Regular Path: Existing component's fx_snapshot_rate remains 83.00; any INR-converted reporting for that component's historical period still uses 83.00; only newly created components after the change pick up 85.00.
- Stress Variant: A Commercial Change approved the same day the Reference Master rate changes, to confirm the snapshot is taken at the correct transactional moment (component creation within approve_commercial_configuration_version), not at draft time or at report-generation time.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: Reference Master rate update happening concurrently with an in-flight approval transaction; the approval's snapshot must use one consistent rate value, not a torn read.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: transaction_currency on the component is immutable post-creation; fx_snapshot_rate is immutable post-creation; both confirmed by attempting (and expecting rejection of) a direct update.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Reports/detail views clearly label which FX rate was used and as-of when, avoiding the false impression that INR values auto-update with market rates.
- Historical Variant: Historical component from a year prior still shows its original snapshot rate, not today's rate, when viewed today.
- Expected Business Result: Financial history is never silently revalued by later FX movements.
- Expected Technical Invariants: fx_snapshot_rate and transaction_currency are write-once fields.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: D-011
- Notes: N/A

### E-001: Create a Commercial Change version seeded from currently active components
- Pack: E - Commercial Change
- Business Objective: Confirm createVersionFromActive correctly seeds a new draft from exactly the currently active (open) components, not stale or superseded ones.
- Domain: Commercial Change
- Object / Record Type: commercial_configuration_versions, commercial_components
- Starting State: Configuration is on Version 2 (active), with Version 1 fully superseded.
- Personas: Finance Analyst
- Preconditions: create_commercial_configuration_version called with change_category = renewal.
- Regular Path: New draft is created, request_id assigned, status = draft, seeded fields reflect exactly Version 2's open components (not Version 1's superseded ones).

- Historical Variant: N/A

- Expected Technical Invariants: N/A (this journey exists specifically to characterize an area with no confirmed protective invariant)

### G-001: MUG unit-quantity floor applied when actual usage falls below threshold

## Pack H: Go Live

### H-001: Create Go Live Request, Happy Path
- Pack: H - Go Live
- Business Objective: A recurring commercial line item's monthly entitlement allocation can be authorized to begin once its commercial configuration version is approved.
- Domain: Go Live
- Object / Record Type: go_live_requests (status = draft)
- Starting State: Recurring commercial line item exists; its commercial_configuration_versions row has status = approved.
- Personas: Finance Ops Analyst (creator)
- Preconditions: Commercial version approved; line item is recurring (not on-demand); no active (non-cancelled) go_live_requests row already exists for the stable_component_key.
- Regular Path: Analyst opens the line item, invokes create_go_live_request with goLiveDate, prorateFirstMonth, commercialConfigurationId, commercialVersionId; system assigns requestNumber (GLR-000123 format), stableComponentKey copied from commercial_components, status = draft.
- Stress Variant: Create request immediately after version approval completes (no propagation delay expected since read is live, not cached).
- Authorization Variant: Only users with go_live write/create permission can invoke create_go_live_request.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A (single insert, no prior row to race against)
- Idempotency Variant: N/A (each call intentionally creates a new draft row)
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: requestNumber is unique and sequential; stableComponentKey matches the line item's current commercial_components.stable_component_key exactly.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Line item's Go Live tab shows the new draft with correct derived LineItemGoLiveStatus = NO_GO_LIVE (draft does not count as pending).
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: A governed draft request exists; no entitlement or billing effect yet.
- Expected Technical Invariants: go_live_requests.commercial_configuration_versions.status was 'approved' at insert time; status = 'draft'; customerConfirmationStatus = 'pending'.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: H-002, H-003, H-031
- Notes: N/A

### H-004: Save Draft with Optimistic Row-Version Lock, Single Editor
- Pack: H - Go Live
- Business Objective: Draft edits persist safely and advance the row version for later conflict detection.
- Domain: Go Live
- Object / Record Type: go_live_requests (status = draft)
- Starting State: Existing draft request, known rowVersion.
- Personas: Finance Ops Analyst
- Preconditions: Draft exists; analyst has current rowVersion from last read.
- Regular Path: Analyst edits goLiveDate or prorateFirstMonth and calls save_go_live_request_draft with expected_row_version matching current row; save succeeds and rowVersion increments.
- Stress Variant: Rapid sequential saves (multiple autosave triggers) each carrying the freshly returned rowVersion.
- Authorization Variant: Only the creator or another user with go_live write permission on drafts can save.
- Concurrency Variant: See H-005 for the conflicting case.
- Idempotency Variant: Re-saving identical field values with the correct expected_row_version still increments rowVersion (not a true no-op by design).
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Prior field values are not silently lost; updated_at (or equivalent) reflects the save time.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: If save fails mid-request (network drop), retry with same expected_row_version succeeds once, and a second identical retry fails with a version mismatch (proving the first actually landed).
- UX Checks: UI reflects the new rowVersion after save so the next edit's lock check does not spuriously fail.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Draft content evolves without corrupting other fields.
- Expected Technical Invariants: rowVersion is monotonically increasing per successful write.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: H-001
- Related Journeys: H-005
- Notes: N/A

### H-005: Draft Row-Version Conflict, Two-Tab Concurrent Edit
- Pack: H - Go Live
- Business Objective: Prevent a stale-tab edit from silently overwriting another user's (or the same user's other tab's) newer draft edit.
- Domain: Go Live
- Object / Record Type: go_live_requests (status = draft)
- Starting State: Draft open in two browser tabs/sessions with the same initial rowVersion.
- Personas: Finance Ops Analyst (same user, two tabs) or two Finance Ops Analysts
- Preconditions: Draft exists; both sessions loaded the same rowVersion N.
- Regular Path: Tab A saves successfully, rowVersion becomes N+1. Tab B then attempts save_go_live_request_draft with expected_row_version = N; call fails with an optimistic-lock conflict rather than overwriting Tab A's change.
- Stress Variant: Both tabs submit within the same millisecond (race at the database level, not just application level).
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This journey is itself the concurrency case.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Tab A's saved values are never lost; no row is left in an inconsistent partial-merge state.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Tab B reloads the current row, sees Tab A's changes, and can re-apply its own edits on top with a fresh rowVersion.
- UX Checks: Tab B surfaces a clear "this record changed elsewhere, reload to continue" message rather than a generic 500 or, worse, a silent success.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: No lost-update bug on concurrent draft editing.
- Expected Technical Invariants: expected_row_version mismatch reliably rejects the write at the database/RPC layer, not merely in client-side code that could be bypassed.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: H-004
- Related Journeys: H-033
- Notes: Per the cross-cutting grounding note, verify current db-push state: confirm the expected_row_version check in save_go_live_request_draft is actually deployed to the live database and not merely present in application code awaiting a migration push. Treat as unverified until confirmed.

- Recovery/Resilience Variant: If submit fails after partially updating workflow state (simulated failure), the request remains cleanly in draft, not a hybrid state.

### H-007: Send Back Go Live Request with Reason
- Pack: H - Go Live
- Business Objective: Allow a reviewer to return a submitted request for correction instead of approving or blindly rejecting.
- Domain: Go Live
- Object / Record Type: go_live_requests (submitted -> sent_back)
- Starting State: Request submitted, currentWorkflowNodeKey pointing at a reviewer's node.
- Personas: Workflow Node Reviewer (team member)
- Preconditions: Reviewer is an active member of the current node's responsible team; reason text provided.
- Regular Path: Reviewer calls send_back_go_live_request with a non-empty reason; status becomes sent_back; sentBackBy/At/Reason recorded.
- Stress Variant: Very long reason text (near any UI/DB field limit) still persists intact.
- Authorization Variant: A user who is not a member of the responsible team is rejected.
- Concurrency Variant: Reviewer sends back at the same moment another reviewer approves; only one transition should win, the other should fail cleanly against the expected_current_node_key guard.

### H-011: Approve Go Live Request, Happy Path
- Pack: H - Go Live

- Preconditions: All of the above preconditions satisfied simultaneously; this is a single-node workflow (or the final node) so approval finalizes.

- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: The line item's recurring entitlement allocation is authorized to begin at goLiveDate.

### H-043: Direct mutation bypass attempt against go_live_requests.status is blocked
- Pack: H - Go Live
- Business Objective: Confirm a crafted direct write against go_live_requests.status bypassing approve_go_live_request is rejected at the database layer, not merely absent as a UI control, matching the equivalent protection already proven for Customer Master, Commercial Components, and Workflow Versions.
- Domain: Go Live
- Object / Record Type: go_live_requests
- Starting State: A request in submitted or resubmitted status.
- Personas: A user with direct database access attempting to bypass the RPC (adversarial/security-review persona, not a normal product user).
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: N/A (this is a bypass-attempt journey, not a UI path)
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: This is fundamentally an authorization/defense-in-depth journey.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirmed by direct migration inspection (2026-09-16 reconciliation): `go_live_requests` has RLS enabled with `trg_go_live_requests_updated_at`, `trg_audit_go_live_requests`, and `trg_go_live_requests_row_version` triggers, but no `fn_protect_go_live_requests_lifecycle`-style BEFORE-UPDATE guard trigger analogous to `fn_protect_customer_lifecycle` (customers) or `fn_protect_commercial_component_lifecycle` (commercial_components). RLS-with-no-policy blocks the anon/authenticated client roles, but does not stop a write executed as service_role or a direct superuser/db-owner connection, the way a BEFORE-UPDATE trigger would (triggers fire regardless of role; RLS bypass is role-based). This journey should confirm that gap live, not assume it.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: A line item's entitlement allocation can never become Live except through the real, actor-audited approve_go_live_request path.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Based on migration inspection, no protect-trigger currently exists on go_live_requests, unlike the other three domains named above; this is a real, confirmed, currently-open defense-in-depth gap (category A), not merely a documentation absence. It does not allow a normal application user to bypass approval (RLS blocks the anon/authenticated roles same as everywhere else); the exposure is specifically to anyone with direct service_role or superuser database access, a materially narrower and lower-likelihood threat than a missing RLS policy would be.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: B-017, D-011, L-003, L-017
- Notes: Reconciled 2026-09-16: confirmed via direct migration inspection, not merely flagged as a suspicion during gap analysis. Downgraded from P0 to P1 because the realistic exposure is narrower than initially framed (RLS already blocks the anon/authenticated attack surface that a normal user or a compromised client session could reach; only a privileged database connection could exploit the missing trigger). Still a real, worth-fixing gap, just not a P0-level authorization bypass reachable through the product's own UI or API.

### J-001: Start Node Transparent Pass-Through on Submit
- Pack: J - Workflow Runtime
- Business Objective: Confirm the Start node never itself requires an action and submission always resolves forward to the first real gate.
- Domain: All four governed domains (customer_onboarding, customer_change, commercial_configuration, go_live)
- Object / Record Type: workflow_definition_versions graph; governed request row of each domain
- Starting State: Published graph with Start -> (optional form_step) -> Approval -> End; request in draft, not yet submitted.
- Personas: Requestor (Finance Ops Analyst)
- Preconditions: Active definition with a published version exists for the domain.
- Regular Path: Requestor submits; fn_resolve_workflow_next_approval is called with from_node_key = null and resolves the first Approval node, skipping over Start (and any interposed form_step) automatically; current_workflow_node_key is set to that Approval node's key.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: workflow_node_transitions gets one row with action=submit, from_node_key=Start's key (or null), to_node_key=the resolved Approval node key.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Timeline shows the submit transition landing directly on the first Approval stage, no visible "Start" stage lingering in the UI.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Requestor never has to take any action at Start; the graph engine transparently walks past it.
- Expected Technical Invariants: current_workflow_node_key after submit always equals a node of type approval, never start or form_step.
- Priority: P2
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: J-016, J-023
- Notes: N/A

### J-006: Decision Node With No Fallback and No Match Raises WORKFLOW_DECISION_NO_MATCH
- Pack: J - Workflow Runtime
- Business Objective: Confirm the engine fails safe (loud error) rather than silently stalling when a decision node has no fallback and no condition matches.

- Starting State: Commercial version's segment=mid_market.

- Regular Path: Requestor attempts submit; neither conditioned edge matches and there is no fallback; RPC raises WORKFLOW_DECISION_NO_MATCH; no current_workflow_node_key is set, request remains unsubmitted (or reverts to draft).

- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No workflow_node_transitions row is written for a failed submit.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Requestor cannot self-recover; a Builder admin must edit the graph (add a fallback or an equals/not_equals edge covering mid_market) and publish a new version before the request can be resubmitted successfully against a version that resolves.

- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: A structurally underspecified decision graph blocks submission rather than corrupting routing, at the cost of the requestor being stuck until an admin intervenes.
- Expected Technical Invariants: WORKFLOW_DECISION_NO_MATCH is raised deterministically for every segment value outside the modeled set when no fallback exists.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: J-005, J-025
- Notes: This is a real, currently-possible admin misconfiguration trap worth explicit regression coverage since publish-time validation does not require a fallback to exist.

### J-012: Deactivating a Team Does Not Block Its Members From Approving
- Pack: J - Workflow Runtime

- Regular Path: Deactivated team's still-active member attempts to approve; fn_require_workflow_team_membership only checks user_teams.revoked_at (null, i.e. not revoked) and succeeds, ignoring teams.is_active entirely; approval proceeds normally.

- Historical Variant: N/A

- Business Objective: Confirm that revoking an individual's user_teams row while a request sits at their node's approval step removes their eligibility on the very next attempt.
- Domain: Any governed domain (representative: customer_onboarding)
- Object / Record Type: user_teams row; onboarding case parked at a node
- Starting State: User is an active member of the node's responsible team; request is sitting in needs_action at that node.
- Personas: The soon-to-be-revoked member, an admin performing the revocation
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: Admin sets the user's user_teams.revoked_at to now(); the user immediately attempts to approve; fn_require_workflow_team_membership no longer finds a matching row and raises WORKFLOW_TEAM_REQUIRED.
- Stress Variant: Revoke membership in the exact instant between the user loading the approval screen and clicking Approve (race between page load and click).
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: Two other still-active members of the same team remain able to approve normally while the revoked one cannot, confirming per-user (not per-team-wide) precision.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No transition row is written for the rejected attempt.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Error clearly indicates loss of authorization, not a generic failure, ideally prompting a refresh.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Membership changes take effect live, with no caching lag, which is the correct and safe behavior.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Eligibility is always re-checked live at action time, never cached from page load.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A

- Notes: N/A

### J-015: WORKFLOW_GRAPH_DEAD_END When Current Node Has No Outgoing Path
- Pack: J - Workflow Runtime
- Business Objective: Confirm the distinct dead-end failure mode that fires when current_workflow_node_key is non-null but the graph has a validation gap (e.g. an Approval node with no outgoing edge to anything, not even End).
- Domain: go_live
- Object / Record Type: workflow_definition_versions graph with an Approval node missing any outgoing edge (a gap that current publish-time validation does not catch since it is not decision-specific)
- Starting State: Request currently sitting at that Approval node, about to be approved.
- Personas: Approver
- Preconditions: Graph published in this structurally incomplete state.
- Regular Path: Approver approves; the engine attempts to resolve the next node from this current node and finds none; WORKFLOW_GRAPH_DEAD_END is raised; the approval is not recorded and current_workflow_node_key is not advanced.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No transition row for the failed advancement; the request remains parked exactly where it was, re-attemptable once the graph is fixed.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: A Builder admin must add the missing outgoing edge in a new draft and publish; but per L's binding rules, this ALREADY-IN-FLIGHT request never re-resolves to the new version, so this specific stuck request can never actually recover through a graph fix alone.
- UX Checks: Approver sees an unexpected failure on an action that looked otherwise valid (they held permission and were on the right team).
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Confirms a genuine "orphaned forever" class of request distinct from J-011's team-emptiness gap: this one is unrecoverable even with a graph fix once the request already exists, since workflow_version_id is bound at creation.
- Expected Technical Invariants: WORKFLOW_GRAPH_DEAD_END raised deterministically; current_workflow_node_key unchanged after the failed attempt.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: J-011, J-014, L-011
- Notes: This combination (validation gap in a published graph plus permanent version-binding) makes an existing in-flight request genuinely unrecoverable; worth flagging as a product gap needing either stronger publish-time validation or an admin override path to rebind an in-flight request to a corrected version.

### J-026: Concurrent Approve and Send-Back Race Resolved Purely by Row Lock, Not by the Optional Param
- Pack: J - Workflow Runtime
- Business Objective: Confirm that when one approver attempts Approve and a second eligible approver simultaneously attempts Send Back on the very same node, the database's FOR UPDATE lock plus current-node recheck (not client-side param passing) is what deterministically picks a single winner.
- Domain: customer_onboarding
- Object / Record Type: Onboarding case at a shared Approval node with two eligible team members
- Starting State: Both actors have the page open simultaneously; neither has passed p_expected_current_node_key.
- Personas: Approver A (attempts Approve), Approver B (attempts Send Back), same node, same instant
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: Both calls race; the database serializes them via the row's FOR UPDATE lock; whichever transaction commits first wins and advances/reverts current_workflow_node_key and workflow_cycle_number accordingly; the second call's re-check of current_workflow_node_key against the now-changed row fails and it is rejected.
- Stress Variant: Repeat with 5 simultaneous mixed approve/send_back/reject calls from 5 different eligible actors against the same row to confirm exactly one wins and the other four are cleanly rejected with no partial state corruption.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This journey is itself the concurrency variant.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Exactly one workflow_node_transitions row is appended for this contested hop; row_count(competing calls) - 1 calls are rejected with zero side effects.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: The four (or one) rejected actors, upon refreshing, see the row's true new state and can act correctly from there.
- UX Checks: Rejected actors see a clear "this was already acted on" message, not a silent failure or a duplicate action applied.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: No matter how many simultaneous conflicting actions are attempted, exactly one takes effect and the resource's state is never corrupted.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Postgres row-level locking guarantees serialization; no lost-update or double-apply is possible.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: J-021
- Notes: N/A
