### K-010: Concurrent Editors, Second Save Is Rejected as Stale Rather Than Silently Discarding the First Save (regression)
- Pack: K - Workflow Builder
- Business Objective: Prove `save_workflow_version_graph` now rejects a stale concurrent whole-graph save with `WORKFLOW_VERSION_DRAFT_STALE` instead of silently letting the second admin's save destructively replace the first admin's committed graph (migration `20260922000000_optimistic_locking_extension.sql`, confirmed applied in the live migration ledger).
- Domain: Workflow Builder
- Object / Record Type: workflow_definition_versions (draft), its nodes/edges
- Starting State: Admin A and Admin B both open the same draft version's canvas at the same time, both starting from the same loaded `row_version`.
- Personas: Admin A, Admin B (both hold write permission)
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: Admin A adds Node X and saves; the whole-graph replace succeeds and `row_version` increments. Admin B, still holding the pre-save `row_version`, makes an unrelated edit (e.g. renames Node Y) and attempts to save; confirm the call is rejected with `WORKFLOW_VERSION_DRAFT_STALE` before any delete-and-reinsert happens, so Node X is never touched.
- Stress Variant: Repeat with both admins editing the SAME node's properties differently; confirm the second, stale save is rejected outright rather than "winning" with different values.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This journey is itself the concurrency variant; it is the central risk this pack previously flagged as unmitigated.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm Node X still exists in the draft after Admin B's rejected save; confirm `row_version` incremented exactly once, from Admin A's successful save only; confirm no partial delete-then-reinsert state was ever visible to a concurrent reader, since the stale save is rejected before the whole-graph replace begins.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Admin B reloads the canvas to the current graph and `row_version`, reapplies the Node Y rename, and saves successfully; confirm this reload-and-reapply path preserves both admins' work.
- UX Checks: Admin B sees an actionable "This workflow draft was changed by someone else since you loaded it..." message rather than a silent success.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: No silent data loss when two Workflow Admins edit the same draft graph concurrently.
- Expected Technical Invariants: `save_workflow_version_graph` compares `p_expected_row_version` against the current `workflow_definition_versions.row_version` under a row lock and raises `WORKFLOW_VERSION_DRAFT_STALE` on mismatch before performing its whole-graph delete-and-reinsert, mirroring the same pattern applied to the other three domains' drafts.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: K-009, K-029, L-015, V-011
- Notes: Reconciled 2026-09-16: previously catalogued as a genuine, unmitigated silent data-loss risk with an explicit recommendation to add optimistic locking. That recommendation has since been implemented and is confirmed applied via the live Supabase migration ledger (version `20260922000000`). Downgraded from P0 to P1; this is now a regression guard. K-029 (concurrent discard vs. edit) remains a distinct, still-open scenario this fix does not address, since discard is a different code path from save.

### K-029: Concurrent discard removes a draft graph an editor is actively editing
- Pack: K - Workflow Builder
- Business Objective: Confirm the outcome when one admin discards a Workflow Builder draft version while a second admin is mid-edit on that same draft, distinct from the existing two-admins-editing-the-same-draft race and the discard-vs-published-version case.
- Domain: Workflow Builder
- Object / Record Type: workflow_definition_versions (status: draft)
- Starting State: A draft version exists and is open for editing in two separate admin sessions.
- Personas: Workflow Admin A (editing), Workflow Admin B (discarding)
- Preconditions: Both admins hold workflow_definition.write.
- Regular Path: Admin A opens the draft canvas and begins editing (not yet saved). Admin B calls discard on the same draft id. Admin A then calls Save Draft Graph.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This is the concurrency variant; the discard and the pending save race against each other.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm whether Admin A's save errors cleanly with a not-found/discarded message, or whether it silently resurrects a draft row, or leaves orphaned node/edge rows referencing a deleted version id.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Admin A should see a clear, actionable message and be able to start a fresh draft rather than being stuck on a dead reference.
- UX Checks: Admin A's canvas should not appear to succeed while actually writing to nothing.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: No orphaned graph data; Admin A is clearly told their draft was discarded by someone else.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Save Draft Graph against a discarded/nonexistent version id fails predictably, never silently no-ops or recreates state.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: V-011, K-018, L-017
- Notes: Added during gap analysis. Materially distinct from V-011 (concurrent save vs save) and the discard-vs-published-immutability cases, since the failure mode here is save-against-a-deleted-target.

### K-030: Stale-draft Refresh reloads the whole page, not just the error banner (regression)
- Pack: K - Workflow Builder
- Business Objective: Prove the Builder's stale-draft Refresh control actually replaces the canvas's own node/edge state with the true current graph, not merely the visible error message, so a subsequent save cannot silently overwrite another admin's real change.
- Domain: Workflow Builder
- Object / Record Type: workflow_definition_versions (draft), its nodes/edges, the canvas editor's local React state
- Starting State: Admin A's canvas has just been rejected with WORKFLOW_VERSION_DRAFT_STALE (as in K-010) after Admin B's concurrent save landed first.
- Personas: Admin A (recovering from staleness), Admin B (whose change must survive)
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: Admin A clicks Refresh; confirm the canvas now displays Admin B's actual latest node/edge content (not Admin A's stale in-memory copy); Admin A reapplies their own edit against this fresh state and saves; confirm both admins' changes are present afterward.
- Stress Variant: Repeat the stale-reject-refresh-reapply cycle multiple times in a row (a third, fourth admin change landing between each Refresh) to confirm the canvas is genuinely re-derived fresh every time, not cached from the first refresh.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This is a direct continuation of K-010's own concurrency scenario, testing the recovery path specifically rather than the initial rejection.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: After Admin A's post-refresh save, the persisted node/edge rows must reflect Admin B's real content plus Admin A's reapplied edit, never a reversion to Admin A's pre-refresh stale copy.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: This entire journey is a recovery-path journey.
- UX Checks: The Refresh control's label and behavior should not imply safety it does not deliver; a control that clears an error without truly reloading state is worse than no control at all, since it creates false confidence.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: No admin's real, saved change can be silently discarded by another admin's stale-recovery click.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Refresh forces the canvas's node/edge state to be re-derived from a fresh server fetch (not left in a previously-initialized local state that a changed prop does not automatically reset).
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: K-010
- Related Journeys: K-010, V-011
- Notes: Discovered live during Batch 1 execution (2026-09-16) while re-verifying K-010's fix: the Refresh button originally called router.refresh(), which cleared the error banner but left the canvas's own useState-held nodes/edges unchanged (deliberately decoupled from props so unrelated re-renders never wipe an admin's in-progress edits), so a subsequent save silently reverted Admin B's real change back to Admin A's stale copy even though the row_version check matched. Fixed in the same Batch 1 pass by switching Refresh to a full page reload; re-verified live that both admins' changes now survive a full stale-reject-refresh-reapply-save cycle.

### M-021: CanApprove OR-Imprecision Combined With a Coincidental Team Match Does Leak an Item Into Pending-My-Approval
- Pack: M - My Work / Approvals / Waiting on Others
- Business Objective: Isolate and confirm the actual risk scenario implied by the documented imprecision, a viewer who holds only ONE domain's approve permission but happens to ALSO be a genuine member of the responsible team for a DIFFERENT domain's item, sees that other-domain item as pending-my-approval even though their permission is not truly scoped to that domain's request type.
- Domain: customer_onboarding (viewer's actual permission) and customer_change (the leaking item)
- Object / Record Type: A customer_change_requests item at a node whose responsible_team_id is a team the viewer happens to genuinely belong to (e.g. a cross-functional Finance team used as the responsible team in both domains' graphs)
- Starting State: Viewer holds onboarding approve permission only, NOT change approve permission, but IS a real member of the team assigned to this change-request node.
- Personas: Viewer with onboarding-only formal permission, incidentally on the right team for a change-domain node
- Preconditions: canApprove's OR-based computation is confirmed to make no per-domain distinction once ANY qualifying permission is held.
- Regular Path: canApprove evaluates true (OR-imprecision); isResponsibleTeam ALSO evaluates true (genuine team match); the item incorrectly appears as pending my approval for a domain the viewer does not actually hold approve rights in.
- Stress Variant: The viewer actually attempts to approve; determine whether the RPC-level permission check (which is presumably scoped correctly per domain, unlike the list computation) catches and rejects this at the point of action, meaning the leak is a list-display-only issue, not an actual authorization bypass; this distinction is the crux of the finding and should be explicitly confirmed either way.
- Authorization Variant: This journey is itself the authorization variant, and the key risk journey for the documented imprecision.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: N/A
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: If the RPC does reject the actual approve action, the UX experience (list says actionable, action fails) mirrors M-011's finding and should be reported the same way.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: At minimum this causes a confusing/misleading list entry; at worst (if the RPC-level check is ALSO imprecise) it could be a genuine cross-domain authorization leak, which must be explicitly ruled out, not assumed.
- Expected Technical Invariants: N/A
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: M-020, M-011
- Notes: This is the single most important journey in Pack M given the grounding brief's explicit callout of this imprecision; the outcome (list-only cosmetic issue vs actual RPC-level bypass) must be empirically determined and reported either way.

### N-031: usage.read and entitlement_settlement.read are real, independent read gates
- Pack: N - Users / Roles / Permissions

- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm the page-level AuthGate admits a session holding any of entitlement.read/usage.read/entitlement_settlement.read, and that each section (Entitlement Sources/Schedule/Ledger vs Monthly Usage vs Unbilled/Unearned Ledger) checks the specific permission documented in AUTHORIZATION_MODEL.md §23.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A

- Historical Variant: N/A

An entitlement.read holder is completely unaffected (still sees everything, per AUTHORIZATION_MODEL.md §23's permission-to-section mapping).
- Expected Technical Invariants: AuthGate's requiredPermission now accepts a list of alternatives ("any of" semantics); the entitlement page passes all three read permissions as alternatives, then gates each section individually. See AUTHORIZATION_MODEL.md §23 for the exact mapping.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: I-025, I-026
- Notes: Reconciled 2026-09-16 as a confirmed gap (category A at the time), then decided and closed in the Product Gap Closure pass following the Batches 3-6 triage (decision: wire up real gates rather than remove the two permissions). Re-run this journey to confirm the new section-visibility mapping, not to rediscover the original gap.

### O-005: Deactivating a team does NOT block its existing members from approving in-flight requests
- Pack: O - Teams
- Business Objective: Surface the real, confirmed inconsistency where fn_require_workflow_team_membership checks only user_teams.revoked_at, never teams.is_active, so a deactivated team's members can still approve.
- Domain: Team, Workflow
- Object / Record Type: teams, user_teams, workflow request
- Starting State: A request is sitting at an Approval node whose responsible team is Team X; Team X has an active member M; a request awaits approval.
- Personas: team_admin (deactivates the team), M (still-active member, e.g. checker)
- Preconditions: Team X is deactivated (is_active = false) while M's own user_teams membership remains unrevoked.
- Regular Path: Admin deactivates Team X entirely; M, still an unrevoked member of Team X, opens the pending request and successfully approves it; the approval succeeds because fn_require_workflow_team_membership only checks M's own revoked_at, not Team X's is_active flag.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Approval is recorded normally, attributed to M, with no error or warning that the responsible team was deactivated at approval time.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: No warning is shown to M that their team is deactivated org-wide.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: This is a real, likely-unintended-looking inconsistency: an admin who believes deactivating a team fully "locks it down" is wrong; only individually revoking each member's own team membership actually blocks approval.
- Expected Technical Invariants: fn_require_workflow_team_membership's WHERE clause references user_teams.revoked_at IS NULL only; it never joins/filters on teams.is_active.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: O-004, O-009, O-015
- Notes: Catalogued as a confirmed real behavior per the grounding brief, not an invented defect; recommend flagging to product owners regardless of whether it is deemed "working as intended."

### O-011: Set a team membership as primary
- Pack: O - Teams
- Business Objective: Let a user designate which of their multiple team memberships is their primary one (e.g. for default routing or display).

- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: The RPC locks the user's active rows (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) before revoking/inserting, so two concurrent promote calls for the same user serialize rather than racing.
- Idempotency Variant: Re-setting the same membership as primary is a no-op (returns the existing row unchanged).
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm the user remains an active member of BOTH the old and new primary team after promotion (only the primary designation moves); confirm at most one active primary per user throughout (uq_user_teams_one_active_primary).
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: The "Make Primary" control appears only on non-primary active team badges; disappears from the old primary team's badge and appears there instead after a swap.
- Historical Variant: The old primary row is revoked (not deleted) and a new non-primary row is inserted for that same team, preserving full history per fn_protect_team_grant's immutable-grant-record invariant.
- Expected Business Result: [CLOSED, Product Gap Closure Batches 3-6] User has a clear default team association, and admins can actually change it after the fact.
- Expected Technical Invariants: set_primary_team_membership (migration 20260930030000, corrected by 20260930040000) atomically revokes the old primary row and reinserts it as non-primary (never dropping the membership), then revokes and reinserts the target row as primary. Confirmed live: the previous primary team remains an active, non-primary membership after a promotion, not removed.
- Priority: P3
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: O-012, O-013
- Notes: Originally confirmed as a real gap (Batch 5): assign_user_to_team's idempotency check silently no-op'd a promotion attempt with no error. Closed in the Product Gap Closure pass; the invariant (one primary per user, globally, per the existing uq_user_teams_one_active_primary partial unique index) was already unambiguous, so no product decision was needed, only the missing swap mechanism.

### O-015: Team membership removed while the approval page is open (PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 5)
- Pack: O - Teams
- Business Objective: Confirm real-time enforcement, not cached membership, at the moment of approval.
- Domain: Team, Workflow
- Object / Record Type: user_teams, workflow request
- Starting State: A request sits at an Approval node whose responsible team is Team X; user M is an active Team X member and has the request's review page open.
- Personas: team_admin (revokes membership), M (checker attempting to approve)
- Preconditions: M's browser session and page remain open throughout.
- Regular Path: While M's review page is still open, an admin revokes M's Team X membership (user_teams.revoked_at set); M then clicks Approve; the server-side fn_require_workflow_team_membership check re-evaluates fresh and rejects with WORKFLOW_TEAM_REQUIRED, even though M never reloaded the page and the Approve button was fully rendered and enabled.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This IS the concurrency scenario: revoke lands strictly between page load and click.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No approval record is created; the request remains at the same node, untouched.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: M sees a clear WORKFLOW_TEAM_REQUIRED error, not a generic failure, and the request state does not silently appear to succeed.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: A revoked team membership takes effect immediately, mid-session, with no stale-permission window.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Team membership is checked live at approval time, never cached from page load.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: O-005, O-016, AB-002, AB-030
- Notes: Directly corresponds to PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 5.

### O-018: Last remaining active member of a team removed while a request waits at that team's node (warn but allow) (PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 10)
- Pack: O - Teams
- Business Objective: When removing the last active member of a responsible team would orphan pending work, warn the admin with a real, current count before the removal completes, but never block the removal outright, and always keep the orphaned state visible afterward until an admin recovers it.
- Domain: Team, Workflow
- Object / Record Type: user_teams, workflow request
- Starting State: Team X has exactly one active member, M; a request sits at an Approval node whose responsible team is Team X.
- Personas: team_admin, M
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: Admin attempts to revoke M's Team X membership. Before the removal completes, checkTeamRemovalImpactAction computes the real, current pending-approval count for Team X; if removing M would leave zero active members and at least one pending item, a confirmation dialog shows "This change will leave N pending approval(s) with no eligible approver on Team X. Remove this membership anyway?" and requires explicit confirmation. If confirmed (or if there was no risk to warn about), the removal proceeds exactly as before; the request itself is never auto-reassigned or auto-cancelled.
- Stress Variant: Multiple requests simultaneously stuck at Team X's node: the warning's count reflects the real total, and the Operational Queue surfaces every one of them individually, not just the first.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: The request's status and node remain unchanged, correctly showing it as still pending, not silently cancelled or auto-approved. The membership removal itself remains fully auditable through the existing user_teams historical-grant mechanism (fn_protect_team_grant); no separate, redundant audit event is invented for the warning/confirmation step itself.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Admin assigns a new active member to Team X; that new member can now see and act on the previously stuck request. Separately, the Operational Queue (/operations/queue) surfaces every currently-stuck item with a "No eligible approver" badge, its responsible team's name, and a summary count, discoverable at any later time, not only at the moment of removal.
- UX Checks: The warning is shown only when removal would genuinely leave zero eligible approvers with real pending work; a removal with no such risk proceeds with no interruption, exactly as before this fix.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: [CLOSED, Product Gap Closure Batches 3-6, decision: warn but allow] A team can still be emptied out while carrying live approval responsibility (administrative flexibility is preserved), but the admin sees a real warning first, and the orphaned state is never invisible afterward.
- Expected Technical Invariants: checkTeamRemovalImpact (src/platform/approvals/server.ts) computes remainingActiveMembers and pendingApprovalCount from the same loadApprovalInbox read every other operational surface shares; OperationalQueueEntry.hasEligibleApprover/responsibleTeamName (src/platform/approvals/domain/operational-queue.ts) surface the same signal on an existing, already-discoverable page rather than a new dashboard.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: O-005, O-009, N-007
- Notes: Directly corresponds to PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 10. Originally recorded as a real, unhandled gap (Batch 6); the Product Gap Closure triage classified it as needing a product decision among block/warn/passive-indicator, and the decision (warn but allow, plus a passive Operational Queue indicator) was implemented and confirmed live: revoking a real team's last two members while a real item was pending correctly showed "1 item has no eligible approver" with the team name and recovery guidance, then cleared immediately on restoring membership.

### O-019: User moves from one team to a different team between two approval levels of the same workflow (PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 11)
- Pack: O - Teams
- Business Objective: Confirm a mid-flight team change for a user is correctly reflected at each subsequent approval level, using live membership at the time each level is reached, not membership as of request creation.
- Domain: Team, Workflow
- Object / Record Type: user_teams, workflow request
- Starting State: A multi-step workflow: level 1 approval is responsible to Team Finance, level 2 approval is responsible to Team Legal; user M starts as an active Finance member and not a Legal member.
- Personas: team_admin, M
- Preconditions: The request must have at least two sequential approval levels bound to two different teams.
- Regular Path: M approves at level 1 as a Finance member; before the request reaches level 2, admin revokes M's Finance membership and grants M an active Legal membership; when the request reaches level 2 (now responsible to Legal), M can approve it as a Legal member, correctly reflecting M's membership at that later point in time, not at request creation or at level 1.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: If M had NOT been granted Legal membership, M correctly cannot act at level 2 despite having approved level 1.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: The audit trail correctly shows M's level 1 approval attributed under the Finance responsibility and M's level 2 approval (if it occurs) attributed under Legal, each reflecting membership at the time of that specific action.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: This journey's audit trail IS a historical-correctness check by nature.
- Expected Business Result: Team responsibility is evaluated fresh at each workflow level, never inherited or fixed from an earlier level.
- Expected Technical Invariants: fn_require_workflow_team_membership is evaluated independently at each node/level against current membership, with no assumption of continuity between levels for the same person.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: O-009, O-015
- Notes: Directly corresponds to PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 11.

- Expected Business Result: Financial truth already committed on an existing commercial component is never silently altered by a later administrative rate change.

### P-013: Attempt to add a new Level 3 System-Supported option (Commercial Nature)
- Pack: P - Reference Masters

A direct add_reference_option RPC call for any of the five Level 3 list_keys (commercial_nature, pricing_model, invoice_timing, slab_method, revenue_recognition_method), bypassing the UI entirely, is now rejected server-side with REFERENCE_LIST_SYSTEM_SUPPORTED.

- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A

- Historical Variant: N/A

- Expected Technical Invariants: add_reference_option (migration 20260930020000_add_reference_option_level3_enforcement.sql) rejects any of the five Level 3 list_keys before insert, regardless of caller. Read access, existing options, and existing references are unaffected; set_reference_option_active (Activate/Deactivate) is deliberately untouched, since Level 3 values may still be deactivated/reactivated.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: P-014, P-015
- Notes: Originally confirmed as a real gap (Batch 6): the UI hid the control but a direct RPC call succeeded unrejected. Closed in the Product Gap Closure pass; the correct behavior was already fully decided and documented (SETTINGS_ARCHITECTURE.md §3), so no product decision was needed, only server-side enforcement matching the already-documented invariant. Automation Feasibility upgraded from PARTIAL to FULL now that the direct server-action/RPC call path is the primary regression check, not merely a UI-absence check.

## Pack R: Audit / Timeline

### R-001: Onboarding Timeline full-tuple verification for an approval action
- Pack: R - Audit / Timeline
- Business Objective: Confirm a meaningful approval action surfaces the complete required tuple in the Timeline.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: RequestTimelineEvent, Onboarding request
- Starting State: An Onboarding request at a workflow node awaiting approval, with a prior revision cycle already completed.
- Personas: Approver, Reviewer/Auditor viewing the Timeline afterward
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: Approver approves with a comment; Timeline entry is created and later verified to convey: actor (approver identity), action (approve), date/time (occurredAt), comment/reason (detail), workflow node (which node this action occurred at), team (approver's team context), workflow version, business object (the request/customer), old value / new value (state transition, e.g. pending -> approved), evidence reference (if applicable), cycle (which approval cycle), and terminal result (if this was the final approval).
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Every element of the required tuple is present and correct in the rendered Timeline entry (variant is not "marker").
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Timeline entry is legible, correctly ordered chronologically among other events.

### S-024: External API v1 authorization, pagination, and identity-parameter boundary
- Pack: S - Search / Navigation / Discovery

- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm calling /api/v1/onboarding/[id] with the human-friendly display id (for example CO-000123) instead of the real stable request id returns a not-found error rather than silently matching the wrong or no record.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A (API surface, not a UI journey)
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: The one real external-facing surface in the product is exercised at least once end to end, not left as an unverified assumption.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Same session-derived identity and requirePermission enforcement as every other Server Action; pagination boundaries clamp rather than error; the documented error contract shape is stable.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: U-015
- Notes: Added during gap analysis. U-015 only confirms the middleware exclusion list doesn't accidentally skip authorization; it never exercises these routes' own pagination, id-matching, or DTO parity boundaries, which this journey covers.

### T-019: Deactivated team still allows its still-assigned members to approve (known inconsistency)
- Pack: T - Settings
- Business Objective: Confirm and document the real, known inconsistency: deactivating a TEAM does not block its still-assigned members from approving at a workflow node bound to that team, since the approval check only reads user_teams.revoked_at, never teams.is_active.
- Domain: Team Master, Workflow Builder, Customer Onboarding (representative consumer of a team-bound node)
- Object / Record Type: Team row, user_teams grant row, workflow node binding
- Starting State: Team "APAC Finance" is active, has Member M as an active (non-revoked) member, and is bound to a workflow node that a request is currently sitting at.
- Personas: Admin who deactivates the team, Member M
- Preconditions: Admin holds team.write; Member M's own user_teams membership is NOT revoked.
- Regular Path: Admin deactivates the "APAC Finance" team itself (teams.is_active=false). Member M, still an active (non-revoked) member per user_teams, opens the pending request and successfully approves it at the team-bound node, exactly as if the team were still active.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: This journey confirms the actual (surprising) authorization outcome rather than the naively-expected one.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: The approval succeeds and is fully recorded in the Timeline as normal, attributed to Member M and the team-bound node.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: To actually block Member M, an admin must separately revoke Member M's user_teams membership (per T-016), not merely deactivate the team.
- UX Checks: No warning is shown to Member M or to the admin that the team is inactive, which may itself be considered a secondary UX gap worth flagging alongside the core inconsistency.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: N/A (this documents a real, confirmed-in-code inconsistency, not an expected-to-pass business outcome)
- Expected Technical Invariants: The workflow-approval eligibility check reads only user_teams.revoked_at; it does not join against or check teams.is_active at all, per the grounding brief.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: T-016, T-018, S-007
- Notes: This is a KNOWN REAL INCONSISTENCY explicitly flagged in the grounding brief, not a hypothesis; write the journey to confirm it reproduces exactly as described, since "deactivating a team" intuitively (but incorrectly) suggests it should block approvals.

## Pack V: Concurrency

### Concurrency Journeys

### V-001: Two draft editors race on the same draft record, stale writer is rejected (regression)
- Pack: V - Concurrency
- Business Objective: Confirm what actually happens today when two makers (or one maker in two tabs) edit the same draft record concurrently, across the shared draft-save mechanism, now that every governed draft's save RPC enforces `p_expected_row_version` staleness checking.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding, Customer Change, Commercial Configuration, Go Live (shared engine mechanism, all four confirmed fixed; domain-specific deep dives are V-012 through V-015)
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_cases / customer_change_requests / commercial_configuration_versions / go_live_requests (draft status)
- Starting State: A single draft record in "draft" status, editable by its creator or any user with edit rights on it.
- Personas: Maker A, Maker B (or Maker A in two browser sessions)
- Preconditions: Draft exists and is not yet submitted; both editors have the draft open with the same loaded `row_version`.
- Regular Path: Maker A opens draft, edits fields, saves; the save succeeds and the draft's row_version increments. Maker B (loaded before A's save, now holding a stale row_version) edits different or overlapping fields and attempts to save after A; confirm the call is rejected with the domain's `*_DRAFT_STALE` error rather than silently overwriting.
- Stress Variant: Repeat with 5 rapid alternating saves from both sides within a few seconds; confirm every stale attempt is rejected, not just the first.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This IS the concurrency variant; core test is that the stale writer is reliably rejected regardless of save ordering.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A (see W-009 duplicate Save Draft for same-payload-twice variant)
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm Maker A's saved edit survives untouched after Maker B's rejected attempt; confirm row_version increments exactly once per accepted save, never on a rejected one.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Maker B reloads to the current row_version and content, reapplies their edit, and saves successfully with no data loss across the cycle.
- UX Checks: Maker B sees the actionable "this was changed by someone else since you loaded it, refresh" message, not a silent success and not a raw RPC error.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: No silent data loss for concurrent draft edits in any of the four governed domains.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Each domain's save RPC compares `p_expected_row_version` against the current row_version under a row lock and raises its own named `*_DRAFT_STALE` error on mismatch (`ONBOARDING_DRAFT_STALE`, `CUSTOMER_CHANGE_DRAFT_STALE`, `COMMERCIAL_VERSION_DRAFT_STALE`, `GO_LIVE_DRAFT_STALE`).
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: V-012, V-013, V-014, V-015, W-009
- Notes: Reconciled 2026-09-16: previously catalogued as a known-but-unfixed gap on the assumption the fix migration was written but not applied. Confirmed via the live Supabase migration ledger that `20260922000000_optimistic_locking_extension.sql` is applied to the actual database, not merely staged as a file. Priority unchanged at P1; reframed from an open-gap verification into a regression journey protecting a fix that is genuinely live today.

### V-002: Two eligible approvers race to approve a Customer Onboarding case
- Pack: V - Concurrency
- Business Objective: Verify the SELECT...FOR UPDATE row lock plus fresh current-node re-check inside approve_customer_onboarding_case actually prevents a double-approval and resulting double Customer Master creation.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_cases
- Starting State: Case awaiting approval at a node with 2+ active team members.
- Personas: Approver A, Approver B (both active members of the responsible team)
- Preconditions: Neither approver is the case's created_by (self-approval block would otherwise short-circuit the test).
- Regular Path: Both approvers open the case and click Approve within milliseconds of each other.
- Stress Variant: Fire both approve RPC calls programmatically with near-zero delay to force true DB-level contention.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: One transaction acquires the row lock first and commits; the second, upon re-checking current_workflow_node_key inside its own transaction, finds the node already advanced and raises WORKFLOW_NODE_ALREADY_ADVANCED (or equivalent) regardless of whether p_expected_current_node_key was passed.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A (see W-011 double Approve on Onboarding for same-actor double-click)
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Exactly one workflow_node_transitions row for this approval step; exactly one Customer Master record created; no duplicate customer with the same identifying details.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: The losing approver sees a friendly "already actioned" message, not a raw DB error.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Exactly one Customer Master record is created from this onboarding case; the case advances exactly once.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Row lock ordering determines the winner deterministically; no partial/duplicate Customer Master rows; no orphaned workflow state.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: V-003, V-004, V-005
- Notes: This is the canonical row-lock race test; the other three domain variants below verify the same mechanism against each domain's materially different terminal mutation.

### V-006: Approve vs Send Back race (two different reviewers, two different actions)
- Pack: V - Concurrency
- Business Objective: Confirm that when one reviewer approves and another sends back the same request at nearly the same instant, exactly one action wins and the record lands in a single, consistent state.

- Object / Record Type: any of the four governed request/version tables

- Preconditions: Neither reviewer is created_by.
- Regular Path: A clicks Approve, B clicks Send Back within milliseconds.
- Stress Variant: Programmatic near-simultaneous RPC calls against the same request id.
- Concurrency Variant: Whichever RPC's transaction commits first wins the row lock; the other's fresh current-node re-check fails with already-advanced, and its action is not applied.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Exactly one workflow_node_transitions row is written for this contested step; no request ends up in an ambiguous or mixed state (e.g. simultaneously "approved" and "sent back").
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Losing reviewer sees a friendly already-actioned message and, on refresh, sees the record's true resulting state.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Record ends in exactly one of the two states, never a hybrid; whichever action committed first is authoritative.
- Expected Technical Invariants: current_workflow_node_key and workflow_cycle_number reflect exactly one consistent transition; no duplicate audit rows.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A

- Notes: Applies identically across all four domains; the interesting property is the race mechanism, not the domain-specific terminal mutation, so this is deliberately a single shared journey per the anti-duplication guidance.

### V-009: Maker edits resubmission draft while reviewer is mid-approve-action
- Pack: V - Concurrency
- Business Objective: Confirm a maker editing a sent-back draft cannot silently corrupt the very approval action a reviewer is executing on the prior cycle's snapshot.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding, Customer Change, Commercial Configuration, Go Live
- Object / Record Type: any of the four governed request/version tables
- Starting State: Request currently sent back to maker (cycle N), maker has it open for edits; due to a UI/permissions edge case (or stale tab) a reviewer also has an approve action in flight for what they believe is a still-pending review.
- Personas: Maker, Reviewer
- Preconditions: Reviewer's approve action targets the correct current node; maker's save targets the draft content only.
- Regular Path: Maker saves an edit; reviewer's approve RPC re-checks current node fresh inside its own transaction.
- Stress Variant: Maker performs several rapid successive saves while reviewer's approve call is in flight.
- Concurrency Variant: Because approve's node-eligibility re-check happens inside the SELECT...FOR UPDATE transaction, a reviewer cannot approve a request that has actually moved back to maker's cycle; if the UI let them attempt it, the RPC itself rejects with a node-mismatch error.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No approval is ever recorded against a cycle the maker has since edited past; workflow_node_transitions accurately reflects the true sequence.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Reviewer sees a clear "this request has changed, please refresh" message rather than a silent success.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: No approval is ever applied to stale content.
- Expected Technical Invariants: The RPC's own node/status re-check is the true safety net, independent of client-side state.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: V-006
- Notes: N/A

### V-010: Admin changes workflow definition while a request is mid-flight on it
- Pack: V - Concurrency
- Business Objective: Confirm an in-flight request is not corrupted or silently misrouted when a Workflow Admin edits the underlying workflow graph (nodes, transitions, responsible teams) while the request is sitting at one of its nodes.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding, Customer Change, Commercial Configuration, Go Live (whichever domain's workflow is being edited)
- Object / Record Type: workflow definitions/graph, current_workflow_node_key on the in-flight request
- Starting State: A live request sitting at node "Review A"; an admin opens the same workflow's draft graph and modifies or removes node "Review A" and/or its responsible_team_id, then publishes.
- Personas: Workflow Admin, Reviewer (on the in-flight request)
- Preconditions: The workflow has both a published (active) version driving the in-flight request and a draft graph being edited.
- Regular Path: Admin edits and publishes a new active workflow version while the request is still bound to the old version's node key.
- Stress Variant: Admin removes the exact node the request is currently sitting at.
- Concurrency Variant: In-flight requests continue to reference their current_workflow_node_key as recorded; publishing a new version does not retroactively re-route already-in-flight requests (verify actual behavior against this expectation).
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm whether the in-flight request's node key becomes orphaned (points to a node key that no longer exists in the newly active graph) and what error, if any, surfaces to the next approver.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: If the request becomes stuck, confirm whether an admin has any recovery path (e.g. manual node reassignment) or whether this is a dead end requiring direct DB intervention.
- UX Checks: Approver attempting to act on an orphaned node sees a clear error, not a silent no-op or crash.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: In-flight requests are never silently lost; if orphaned, the gap is visible and actionable, not silent.
- Expected Technical Invariants: No request is left with a current_workflow_node_key referencing a deleted node without a surfaced error.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A

### V-011: Two admins edit the same Workflow Builder draft graph in two tabs, second save now rejected as stale (regression)
- Pack: V - Concurrency
- Business Objective: Confirm the actual, current outcome of two admins editing the same draft workflow graph concurrently, now that `save_workflow_version_graph` checks `p_expected_row_version` before performing its whole-graph delete-all-then-reinsert (migration `20260922000000_optimistic_locking_extension.sql`, confirmed applied).
- Domain: Workflow Builder (cross-cutting admin surface, not one of the four governed domains itself)
- Object / Record Type: workflow draft graph (nodes, edges, responsible_team_id assignments), workflow_definition_versions.row_version
- Starting State: A draft workflow graph with several nodes; both admins have it open, loaded with the same `row_version`.
- Personas: Workflow Admin A, Workflow Admin B
- Preconditions: Neither has published; both are editing the same draft version.
- Regular Path: Admin A adds/edits nodes and saves; the whole-graph replace succeeds and row_version increments. Admin B, still viewing the pre-A-save graph and row_version, edits differently and attempts to save after A; confirm the call is rejected with `WORKFLOW_VERSION_DRAFT_STALE` before any delete-all-then-reinsert executes.
- Stress Variant: Both admins make many small edits over a few minutes, saving repeatedly and interleaved; confirm every stale attempt is rejected, never silently applied.
- Concurrency Variant: The row-version check now runs before the delete-all-then-reinsert body, so a stale save never reaches the destructive whole-graph replace at all; this is no longer a "certain data loss" outcome.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm Admin A's saved graph is untouched after Admin B's rejected attempt; confirm no orphaned or partially-replaced node/edge rows result from a rejected save, since rejection happens before any delete begins.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: Admin B reloads to the current graph and row_version, reapplies their edit, and saves successfully.
- UX Checks: Admin B sees the actionable "This workflow draft was changed by someone else since you loaded it..." message instead of a silent full discard.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Admin A's work is preserved; Admin B is told clearly and can recover cleanly.
- Expected Technical Invariants: No duplicate/orphaned node or edge rows after either the accepted or the rejected save; graph is always internally consistent at rest; the stale check runs under the same row lock as the save itself.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: V-001, V-010, K-010, K-029
- Notes: Reconciled 2026-09-16: previously catalogued as a guaranteed, deterministic full-replace data-loss outcome distinct from the other domains' probabilistic row_version gap. That distinction no longer holds: Workflow Builder drafts now have the identical row_version staleness guard as the other three domains, confirmed applied via the live migration ledger. K-029 (concurrent discard vs. edit) remains a separate, still-open scenario this fix does not cover.

- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: W-001, W-014
- Notes: This is a same-request-again scenario as described in the grounding brief (double click, refresh-then-repeat), not a distributed idempotency-key retry, since no such infrastructure exists.

### X-011: Regression guard: ambiguous overloaded approve_* RPC signatures must never reoccur

- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Any future migration that changes one of these RPC signatures must include an explicit DROP of the prior overload in the same migration set, verified by this check catching a reintroduction immediately (an ambiguous-function error on call, not silently).
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: If a future migration reintroduces this, the entire approval flow across all four domains breaks in production; this journey exists specifically to catch that before release.
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: This journey documents and guards against a real, already-fixed historical bug.
- Expected Business Result: No ambiguous-function errors on any approve/reject/send-back call, ever again.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Exactly one signature per RPC name across all four domains' workflow functions.

- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: N/A
- Notes: An excellent regression-class journey per the grounding brief; should run on every schema-affecting release, not just once.

## Pack Z: Failure / Recovery / Chaos

### Z-001: Session expires while a draft is being edited
- Pack: Z - Failure / Recovery / Chaos
- Business Objective: Confirm a session expiring mid-edit produces a clear, honest re-authentication prompt without silently losing unsaved work if avoidable, or at minimum without corrupting the persisted draft.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding, Customer Change, Commercial Configuration, Go Live
- Object / Record Type: any of the four governed draft tables, user session
- Starting State: User has a draft open and has been editing for long enough that their session naturally expires.
- Personas: Maker
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: Session expires; user attempts to save.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Save attempt with an expired session is rejected server-side; no partial/corrupted draft write occurs.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: User is prompted to re-authenticate; ideally unsaved edits are preserved client-side (e.g. in local form state) so they can retry the save immediately after re-login.
- UX Checks: Clear "session expired, please log in again" messaging, distinct from the AuthGate's separate "session backend unavailable" message.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: No silent data corruption; user is given a clear path to recover their work.
- Expected Technical Invariants: N/A
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: Z-002
- Notes: N/A

- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: If the session is invalid before the RPC's own auth context is established, the action is rejected entirely, not partially applied.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: User re-authenticates and can confirm the true current state (approved or still pending) before retrying, per the same idempotency guards as W-013.
- UX Checks: Clear re-authentication prompt; no misleading "success" shown for a rejected action.
- Historical Variant: N/A

- Notes: N/A

### Z-003: Network failure after the client sends a request but before the response arrives
- Pack: Z - Failure / Recovery / Chaos
- Business Objective: Confirm a genuine network drop between request-sent and response-received (distinct from a client-side timeout perception) leaves the system in a correct, recoverable state, and the user is not left believing the opposite of what actually happened.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding, Customer Change, Commercial Configuration, Go Live
- Object / Record Type: any of the four governed request/version tables
- Starting State: User submits an action (submit/approve/reject/send back/save draft).
- Personas: Any user
- Preconditions: Network is severed after the server has received the request (simulate via a proxy that drops the response but lets the request through).
- Regular Path: Server completes and commits its transaction; the client never receives confirmation.
- Stress Variant: Also test the network drop occurring BEFORE the server ever receives the request, to confirm the two distinct failure points are handled the same way from the user's perspective (both look identical client-side).
- Idempotency Variant: On reconnect, the user's retry hits the same status-guards described throughout Pack W, so no duplicate mutation occurs regardless of which failure point actually happened.
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Exactly one mutation is ever applied, matching whichever of the two failure points actually occurred.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: User can safely retry; retry resolves to the true current state.
- UX Checks: User is not left on an indefinite spinner; a reasonable client-side timeout eventually surfaces a retry option.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: No lost or duplicated business mutation from a genuine network partition.
- Expected Technical Invariants: N/A
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: W-012, W-013, Z-004
- Notes: N/A

### PRODUCT GAP NOTES (Pack Z addendum)

Gap analysis found no try/catch around the Supabase Auth admin API call backing /settings/user-access (`listAuthUsers`), unlike the equivalent read on the Operational Queue page which explicitly handles this failure mode. Z-030 exists to confirm this empirically rather than assume it crashes; if confirmed, it is a real, fixable resilience gap, not an invented one.

## Pack ACC: Accessibility

This pack exists because docs/UI_SYSTEM.md states a hard requirement (not an aspiration) for full keyboard navigation, visible focus states, labels on icon-only controls, and status that never relies on color alone, yet no journey anywhere else in this catalogue exercises the product without a mouse. This single-journey pack is intentionally small; it is a starting point for a fuller accessibility pass, not a claim of complete coverage.

### ACC-001: Keyboard-only navigation across a full governed approval flow
- Pack: ACC - Accessibility
- Business Objective: Confirm a user with no mouse can complete a full governed action end to end using only the keyboard, per the UI system's stated hard requirement.
- Domain: Cross-cutting (Customer Onboarding, Customer Change, Commercial Configuration, Go Live, Approvals)
- Object / Record Type: Any governed draft/request plus its review/approval screen
- Starting State: A draft exists and a separate approval task is pending.
- Personas: Maker, Checker, both using keyboard-only navigation
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: Tab through a draft form's fields in a sensible order, submit via keyboard (Enter/Space on the focused submit control), then as Checker tab to the pending item, open it, and approve it via keyboard alone.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: The resulting submission/approval is identical in the database to one performed with a mouse; no field is silently skipped by tab order.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Every interactive control has a visible focus ring; icon-only controls (for example a Refresh or an inline action icon) have an accessible label read by a screen reader, not just a tooltip; no status is conveyed by color alone.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: The governed flow is fully completable without a mouse.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Tab order matches visual/logical order; no keyboard trap exists in any modal or drawer used along the way.
- Priority: P2
- Automation Feasibility: MANUAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: N/A
- Notes: Added during gap analysis. This is a starting point, not full accessibility coverage; a dedicated accessibility audit would likely expand this pack considerably.
## Pack AA: Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle

### AA-001: Full lifecycle, Onboarding to Customer Master to Commercial to Go Live to Entitlement
- Pack: AA - Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle
- Business Objective: Verify a single customer can move cleanly end to end from first onboarding submission through to a live, entitled commercial relationship, with each domain's system of record correctly linked to the next.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding, Customer Master, Commercial, Go Live, Entitlement (see Pack D/E/F/G/H/I for deep coverage of Commercial, Go Live, and Entitlement internals)
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case, customers, commercial_configuration_version, go-live record, entitlement record
- Starting State: No case, no customer record exists yet for this prospective customer.
- Personas: Maker, Reviewer/Approver, Go Live operator, Entitlement administrator (see relevant packs for exact role names)
- Preconditions: No hard duplicate blockers; workflow (if any) configured with active team members at every node the case/version will pass through.
- Regular Path: Maker creates and submits an onboarding case (A-001 through A-003); reviewer approves it, atomically creating the customers row plus Commercial Configuration Version 1 (A-011); an approved Commercial Configuration Version exists and is carried into a Go Live process (mechanics owned by Pack F/G); once Go Live completes, the customer's commercial terms become entitled/active (mechanics owned by Pack H/I); confirm at each handoff that the receiving domain correctly reads the exact customer id, commercial configuration id, and version created by the prior step, with no manual re-entry or silent mismatch.
- Stress Variant: A case with the maximum realistic number of commercial components carried all the way through to Go Live and Entitlement.
- Authorization Variant: Confirm the actor performing each domain's step holds that domain's own required permission independently, permission from one domain (e.g. customer.approve) does not implicitly grant capability in another (e.g. whatever Go Live's own permission model requires, per Pack F/G).
- Concurrency Variant: N/A (see AA-006 for concurrent governed requests on an already-live customer)
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: The customer id and commercial configuration/version id are consistent and traceable across every domain's own records; no domain silently creates a duplicate or orphaned reference.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: If Go Live or Entitlement processing fails partway (mechanics per Pack F/G/H/I), confirm the customer and its approved Commercial Configuration Version remain valid and re-attemptable, not corrupted by the partial downstream failure.
- UX Checks: A user following this customer's record from the Onboarding case through to Customer Master, Commercial, and eventually Go Live/Entitlement views should see a coherent, cross-linked narrative, not disconnected records that merely happen to share a customer id.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: The full "prospect to live, entitled customer" journey works end to end with no broken handoff.
- Expected Technical Invariants: The Onboarding-to-Customer-Master-to-Commercial linkage is the one fully specified in this pack's grounding (A-011's atomic transaction); downstream Go Live/Entitlement linkage mechanics are owned by Pack F/G/H/I, described here only at the level of "an approved Commercial Configuration Version exists and flows forward."
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL (full end-to-end automation depends on Go Live/Entitlement domains covered in other packs)
- Dependencies: A-011
- Related Journeys: A-011, A-035, see Pack D/E/F/G/H/I for the Commercial/Go Live/Entitlement legs of this journey
- Notes: Commercial/Go Live/Entitlement internals are intentionally described here only at the "an approved Commercial Configuration Version exists" level of abstraction, per instructions; consult Pack D/E/F/G/H/I for the detailed mechanics of those legs.

### AA-002: Customer Change submitted and approved after Go Live
- Pack: AA - Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle
- Business Objective: Confirm governed field changes (e.g. address, primary contact) remain possible and correctly isolated from commercial/entitlement state once a customer is fully live.
- Domain: Customer Change, Customer Master, Go Live (context only)
- Object / Record Type: customer_change_request, customers
- Starting State: Customer is fully onboarded, commercially configured, and has completed Go Live (per AA-001).
- Personas: Maker, Reviewer
- Preconditions: Customer.is_active === true.
- Regular Path: Maker creates and submits a Customer Change Request (C-001, C-005) against the live customer; approval (C-017) updates only the proposed governed fields on customers; confirm the customer's live commercial configuration and Go Live/entitlement status are completely unaffected by this Customer Master field change, since Customer Change has no authority over commercial/go-live records.
- Stress Variant: A change request proposing fields that might seem commercially adjacent (e.g. billing_currency) still only touches customers, never the Commercial Configuration itself; verify no unintended cross-domain write occurs.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: See AA-006 for the case of a Customer Change request racing with a new Commercial Version on the same live customer.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: customer_field_history correctly attributes the change, fully independent of and non-interfering with commercial/go-live audit trails (which live in their own domains per Pack D/E/F/G).
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: Customer detail page reflects the updated field immediately; Commercial/Go Live views (owned by other packs) remain visually unaffected.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Post-go-live governance of core customer data remains fully functional and correctly scoped.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Customer Change's write scope is strictly the 25 governed fields on customers; it has zero write authority over commercial_configurations or go-live records.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: AA-001, C-017
- Related Journeys: C-017, AA-006, see Pack F/G for Go Live details
- Notes: N/A

### AA-003: New commercial component added after existing components are Live
- Pack: AA - Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle
- Business Objective: Confirm a customer can receive an additional commercial component (e.g. a new product line) after their existing components have already gone live, without disrupting the already-live components.

- Object / Record Type: commercial_configuration_version (new version), existing live components

- Personas: Maker/Approver for the new Commercial Version (exact roles per Pack D/E)
- Preconditions: Customer is active (noting B-011's documented gap that this is NOT actually enforced even if the customer were inactive).
- Regular Path: A new Commercial Configuration Version is created adding the new component, goes through its own approval, and its own Go Live process (mechanics per Pack D/E/F/G); confirm the existing already-live components remain untouched, active, and unaffected by the new version's creation and rollout.
- Stress Variant: The new component shares a naming/key pattern very similar to an existing live component, verify no accidental collision or overwrite.
- Authorization Variant: N/A (delegated to Pack D/E for Commercial's own permission model)
- Concurrency Variant: A Customer Change Request is also in flight on the same customer while this new component is being added (see AA-006).
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: The customer's full commercial history shows both the original version(s) and this new version as a coherent, additive sequence, not a replacement.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: If the new component's Go Live fails, existing live components must remain fully operational and unaffected.
- UX Checks: Commercial view shows a clear version history distinguishing what was live before versus what was newly added.
- Historical Variant: This journey is inherently about additive historical progression of commercial state.
- Expected Business Result: Commercial relationships can grow incrementally over a customer's lifetime without risk to already-live terms.
- Expected Technical Invariants: New version creation is additive; it must never mutate or retroactively alter prior live versions' recorded state.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL (Commercial/Go Live mechanics owned by Pack D/E/F/G)
- Dependencies: AA-001
- Related Journeys: AA-001, AA-006, see Pack D/E for Commercial Version internals

### AA-005: Team rename in Workflow Builder after historical approvals
- Pack: AA - Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle
- Business Objective: Confirm that renaming a responsible team in the Workflow Builder does not retroactively corrupt or misrepresent WHO approved historical onboarding/change decisions, given that actor display names are live-resolved rather than snapshotted at decision time (except for Customer Master's own field-level history).
- Domain: Customer Onboarding, Customer Change, Workflow Builder (cross-cutting)
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (approved historically), customer_change_request (approved historically), team record
- Starting State: An onboarding case and/or change request was approved historically by a member of Team "Finance Ops"; the team is later renamed to "Finance Operations" in Workflow Builder.
- Personas: Workflow Admin (performing the rename), Auditor (reviewing historical decisions)
- Preconditions: At least one historical approval exists that was routed through the now-renamed team.
- Regular Path: Auditor views the historical case/request's decision timeline; since Onboarding/Change Timelines live-resolve actor display names via resolveActorLabels rather than a write-time snapshot (per the grounding brief), confirm the timeline correctly shows the individual APPROVER's name unaffected by the team rename (the approver is a person, not the team itself), and separately confirm whether any team-name label shown in that timeline (e.g. "routed to Finance Ops") updates to reflect the new team name or remains as originally recorded, verify actual behavior against code since this is not explicitly detailed in the grounding brief beyond the general live-resolution pattern.
- Stress Variant: The team is renamed multiple times, and/or the underlying team record is deleted/archived entirely after the rename, verify the historical timeline does not break or show a broken/null reference.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: This IS the audit integrity check: does live-resolution of actor/team labels ever cause a historical decision to appear to have been made by a different, currently-named entity than actually acted at the time, in a way that misrepresents history for compliance purposes.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: If team names in historical timelines DO update live (following the documented live-resolution pattern), the UI should ideally still make clear that the underlying decision routing/permission set at the time may have differed from the team's current composition, to avoid a misleading impression of historical accuracy.
- Historical Variant: This journey is inherently about historical accuracy under a live-resolution display model.
- Expected Business Result: Individual approver attribution remains accurate regardless of team renames (approver identity is a person, immutable); team-label display behavior should be verified and, if it live-updates, flagged as a documented characteristic (not necessarily a bug) since it deviates from field-level snapshot accuracy that Customer Master's own history provides.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Only Customer Master's own Activity/former-name history uses write-time field-level snapshot rows (customer_field_history); Onboarding/Change/Commercial/Go Live timelines live-resolve actor (and likely team) display names, per the grounding brief.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL (requires renaming a team via Workflow Builder and inspecting historical timeline rendering)
- Dependencies: A-011 or C-017 (a historical approval to inspect)
- Related Journeys: AA-013
- Notes: The exact behavior of team-label rendering (live vs. frozen) in historical timelines is not fully specified in the grounding brief; verify against code. This is a candidate for a documented product characteristic rather than a bug, but worth flagging if it produces a misleading audit picture. See PRODUCT GAP NOTES.

### AA-006: One customer with multiple concurrent governed requests
- Pack: AA - Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle
- Business Objective: Confirm the system behaves safely and predictably when a single customer has more than one governed request in flight simultaneously across different domains (e.g. a Customer Change Request AND a new Commercial Version both pending at once).
- Domain: Customer Change, Commercial (see Pack D/E for Commercial internals), Customer Master
- Object / Record Type: customer_change_request, commercial_configuration_version, customers
- Starting State: An active, already-onboarded customer has a Customer Change Request R (proposing e.g. address change) in submitted status AND, independently, a new Commercial Version V (adding a component) also pending approval at the same time.
- Personas: Maker/Reviewer for R, Maker/Reviewer/Approver for V (may be the same or different individuals)
- Preconditions: Both R and V reference the same customer id.
- Regular Path: R is approved first, advancing customers.rowVersion; V's approval process (governed by its own domain's staleness/locking rules per Pack D/E, likely NOT keyed off customers.rowVersion at all since Commercial Versions are their own object) proceeds independently and is approved second; confirm both complete successfully without either corrupting or blocking the other, since they operate on genuinely different tables (customers fields vs. commercial_configuration_version).
- Stress Variant: Three or more concurrent governed requests/versions on the same customer simultaneously (e.g. R, V, and a second Change Request R2 all pending at once).
- Authorization Variant: Different individuals hold approval rights in each domain, confirm cross-domain approvals do not require or imply any single unified sign-off across R and V.
- Concurrency Variant: This IS the concurrency journey; the central risk is whether any shared assumption (e.g. both domains reading the same customers.rowVersion) creates an unintended false-staleness collision between genuinely unrelated requests, or conversely, whether two requests that SHOULD be considered conflicting (e.g. both changing something commercially adjacent) are incorrectly treated as independent.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Final state correctly reflects both R's and V's approved changes with no data loss or overwrite between the two unrelated write paths.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: If V's approval fails or is sent back, R's already-approved change remains intact and vice versa, since these are independent domains.
- UX Checks: A user viewing the customer's unified activity/history (if such a cross-domain view exists) sees both R's and V's outcomes correctly attributed and ordered.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Multiple simultaneous governed workflows on the same customer are a normal, safe, everyday occurrence, not a hazard, as long as they touch genuinely distinct data.
- Expected Technical Invariants: customers.rowVersion staleness checking (C-006) is scoped specifically to Customer Change approvals against the customers table; it does not and should not gate unrelated Commercial Version approvals, which are governed by Pack D/E's own concurrency mechanisms.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL (requires coordinating two domains, one of which is detailed in Pack D/E rather than this brief)
- Dependencies: AA-001, C-005
- Related Journeys: C-006, C-029, AA-003, AA-004
- Notes: N/A

### AA-007: Onboarding case abandoned before any Customer Master record ever exists
- Pack: AA - Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle
- Business Objective: Confirm that a prospective customer who never gets approved leaves absolutely no trace in Customer Master, Commercial, or Go Live, only a cancelled onboarding case remains.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case (cancelled)
- Starting State: Draft onboarding case created, never submitted (or submitted and sent back but never approved).
- Personas: Maker
- Preconditions: No approval has ever occurred for this case.
- Regular Path: Maker cancels the draft case (A-018); confirm across Customer Master, Commercial, and Go Live domains that NO record of any kind (no customers row, no commercial_configuration, no go-live record) was ever created for this prospective customer, since the only creation path is the atomic approval transaction (A-011).
- Stress Variant: The case had extensive data entered (all stages, multiple documents uploaded) before cancellation, confirm the uploaded documents and stage data remain retrievable for audit purposes on the cancelled case itself, while still confirming zero downstream customer/commercial/go-live records exist.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: A direct database-level check confirming zero customers rows reference this case, and the case itself remains a permanent, inspectable record of an abandoned prospect.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: If the business relationship is revisited later, a brand new onboarding case must be created from scratch, there is no "resume" or "convert cancelled case" mechanism implied by the grounding brief.
- UX Checks: Cancelled case is clearly marked as terminal and distinct from any real customer record in any search or list view.
- Historical Variant: This journey is inherently about confirming the absence of history in downstream domains.
- Expected Business Result: The system correctly distinguishes "a prospect we considered and dropped" from "a real customer," with zero real-customer-domain contamination from dropped prospects.
- Expected Technical Invariants: The ONLY path (per A-011) to customers row creation is atomic approval; a cancelled case, by definition, never took that path.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: A-018
- Related Journeys: A-018, AA-008
- Notes: N/A

### AA-008: Onboarding case repeatedly sent back and never approved, then cancelled
- Pack: AA - Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle
- Business Objective: Confirm that a case that undergoes many send-back/resubmit cycles without ever reaching approval still correctly results in zero downstream customer/commercial/go-live artifacts if it is eventually cancelled or simply abandoned, and separately, confirm what recourse exists for a case a reviewer never wants to approve but that also cannot be cancelled once submitted (see A-020's note on the no-reject-state design gap).
- Domain: Customer Onboarding
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case
- Starting State: Case submitted, sent back, resubmitted, sent back again, resubmitted again, multiple cycles, never approved.
- Personas: Maker, Reviewer
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: After several send-back/resubmit cycles, the maker abandons further attempts; since Onboarding has no reject state and cancellation is draft-only (A-020), confirm what the ACTUAL terminal fate of a permanently-stuck, never-to-be-approved, non-draft onboarding case is; verify against code and product design whether any administrative override, forced-cancel, or auto-expiry mechanism exists, or whether such a case is destined to remain in sent_back/resubmitted status indefinitely with no clean terminal state, which would be a genuine design gap.
- Stress Variant: A very high number of send-back/resubmit cycles (5+) to stress-test comment history retention (A-010's historical variant) at scale.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Confirm zero customer/commercial/go-live records exist at every point throughout this cycling, only ever created at the single atomic approval moment.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: This journey is fundamentally about identifying whether a real recovery/termination path exists for a case nobody will ever approve; document the actual answer clearly, since the grounding brief does not specify one.
- UX Checks: If no clean terminal path exists, confirm at minimum that such stuck cases are visible/reportable to admins for manual attention (e.g. a stale-cases report), rather than silently invisible clutter.
- Historical Variant: This is inherently a historical/longevity journey.
- Expected Business Result: A prospect that should never become a real customer is never accidentally approved just to "close it out," and ideally has a genuine terminal fate; if no such fate exists in the product today, that is worth flagging.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Approval remains the sole creation path regardless of how many cycles precede it.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL (the terminal-fate question requires direct product/code verification, not just behavioral observation)
- Dependencies: A-009, A-010, AA-007
- Related Journeys: A-020, AA-007
- Notes: Onboarding's lack of a genuine reject/terminal state for a submitted case that a reviewer never wants to approve is a real, documented design gap (see A-020's Notes); this journey exists to test whether any escape hatch exists in practice. See PRODUCT GAP NOTES.

### AA-014: Row-version locking consistency across all four governed domains (regression)
- Pack: AA - Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle
- Business Objective: Give a single, consolidated cross-domain view confirming draft-staleness protection is now consistent across all four governed domains: `customers.row_version` is a real, wired, cross-transaction lock for approved Customer Master data; each of `customer_onboarding_cases`/`customer_change_requests`/`commercial_configuration_versions`/`go_live_requests`' own draft-save RPCs now independently enforce `p_expected_row_version` staleness checking (migration `20260922000000_optimistic_locking_extension.sql`, confirmed applied via the live Supabase migration ledger). The case-level status machine on these four tables remains protected separately by a pessimistic `SELECT...FOR UPDATE` plus status-text guard, which this journey does not re-test (see the domain approval journeys for that).
- Domain: Customer Onboarding, Customer Change, Commercial Configuration, Go Live, Workflow Builder (cross-cutting)
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case, customer_change_request, commercial_configuration_version, go_live_request, workflow_definition_version, customers
- Starting State: Draft-stage records exist in each of the five draft-bearing surfaces, each potentially open in multiple tabs/sessions simultaneously.
