### AA-015: Duplicate detection does not re-run for GST/PAN entered via Customer Change
- Pack: AA - Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle
- Business Objective: Surface the cross-domain gap that Onboarding's hard-blocking GST/PAN duplicate detection (A-005, A-006) has no equivalent check when the SAME fields are later modified via an approved Customer Change Request, potentially allowing a customer's GST/PAN to be changed into a value that now collides with a different, unrelated customer.
- Domain: Customer Change, Customer Onboarding (comparison only), Customer Master
- Object / Record Type: customer_change_request (proposedValues including gst_number or pan), customers
- Starting State: Two distinct, already-approved customers exist: Customer X with GST "G1", and Customer Y with a different GST. A Customer Change Request is created against Customer Y proposing to change its GST to "G1" (Customer X's existing GST).
- Personas: Maker, Reviewer
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: Maker submits and reviewer approves the change request changing Customer Y's GST to "G1"; per the grounding brief, Customer Change's own submit/approve RPCs are not documented as running the same GST/PAN hard-blocker duplicate check that Onboarding's submit does; confirm via direct testing whether this approval succeeds, resulting in two active customers (X and Y) sharing the identical GST number "G1", a state that Onboarding's own duplicate detection would have prevented at creation time.
- Stress Variant: The same test repeated for PAN instead of GST.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: If this succeeds, it represents a genuine data-integrity/business-risk gap: two legally-distinct customer records sharing a GST/PAN that should be unique per legal entity, undetected by the system after initial onboarding.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: If confirmed, this is a meaningful, previously-undocumented cross-domain gap worth flagging as a recommended enhancement, extend GST/PAN duplicate detection to Customer Change approval, not just Onboarding submission.
- Expected Technical Invariants: N/A, this journey exists to verify whether an invariant (GST/PAN uniqueness across the customer base) that Onboarding enforces at creation is ALSO enforced when the same fields are edited later; per the grounding brief, duplicate detection is stated to occur "at Submit only" in the Onboarding domain specifically, with no equivalent mentioned for Customer Change.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: AA-001 (twice, for Customer X and Customer Y), C-017
- Related Journeys: A-005, A-006, C-017
- Notes: This gap is inferred from the grounding brief's specific scoping of duplicate detection to "Onboarding, at Submit only," with no equivalent described for Customer Change; verify against code whether any such check actually exists in approve_customer_change_request before treating this as a confirmed gap versus a documentation omission. Flagged in PRODUCT GAP NOTES pending verification.

### AA-016: Independent per-domain workflow resolve-once produces different bound versions for the same customer
- Pack: AA - Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle
- Business Objective: Confirm that a single customer's onboarding case and a later change request against that same customer can legitimately be bound to two DIFFERENT workflow versions, if a new version was published in the interim, since each domain resolves its own workflow binding independently and once, per its own case/request creation time.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding, Customer Change (cross-cutting)
- Object / Record Type: customer_onboarding_case, customer_change_request
- Starting State: Workflow version WO1 (applies_to = 'customer_onboarding') is active when the customer's onboarding case is created and later approved. Separately, workflow version WC1 (applies_to = 'customer_change') is active when a later Customer Change Request against this same now-existing customer is created. Between these two events, WC1 is superseded by WC2.
- Personas: Maker, Reviewer, Workflow Admin
- Preconditions: The change request is created AFTER WC2 becomes the active version for the customer_change domain.
- Regular Path: Confirm the change request correctly binds to WC2 (the version active at ITS OWN creation time), completely independent of and unrelated to whichever onboarding workflow version (WO1) governed the original onboarding case, since applies_to scopes these as entirely separate resolve-once bindings; there is no shared or inherited workflow version between the two domains for the same customer.
- Stress Variant: The onboarding case's own workflow, WO1, is ALSO superseded by WO2 at some point, but since the onboarding case is already approved and terminal, confirm this has zero effect on its historical record.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Each domain's request/case correctly and independently records its own resolved workflow_version_id, with no cross-domain leakage or confusion.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: A user viewing this customer's combined history should not be confused by seeing different workflow version references across its onboarding case versus its change requests, this is expected and correct, not an inconsistency bug.
- Historical Variant: This journey is inherently about correct historical workflow-binding independence across domains and over time.
- Expected Business Result: Confirms the resolve-once binding pattern (A-014, C-024) is correctly scoped per-domain-per-record, with no unintended cross-domain coupling.
- Expected Technical Invariants: applies_to scoping ensures customer_onboarding and customer_change workflow resolution are entirely independent processes, even for requests against the exact same customer.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: A-014, C-024
- Related Journeys: A-014, C-024
- Notes: N/A

- Historical Variant: This journey is inherently and entirely historical.
- Expected Business Result: Complete, trustworthy, cross-domain institutional memory for any customer's full lifecycle, essential for compliance and dispute resolution.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Every domain's own audit mechanism (field history, live-resolved timelines, audit_log) remains internally consistent and correctly attributable when assembled together.

### AA-018: Commercial/Go Live records unaffected by later Customer Master deactivation, no cascade
- Pack: AA - Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle

### AA-020: Cross-domain double-click/duplicate-request idempotency
- Pack: AA - Cross-Domain Customer Lifecycle
- Business Objective: Confirm that a user accidentally triggering two near-simultaneous approval requests (e.g. double-clicking Approve, or a flaky network causing a client-side retry) behaves safely and idempotently across every governed domain, not just the ones with an explicitly documented idempotency guarantee.
- Domain: Customer Onboarding, Customer Change, Commercial, Go Live (cross-cutting)
- Object / Record Type: All governed request/case approval actions
- Starting State: A submitted/resubmitted onboarding case and a submitted/resubmitted change request, each ready for approval.
- Personas: Reviewer/Approver (accidental double-action)
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: Reviewer double-clicks Approve (or the client issues a duplicate network request) for both the onboarding case (A-032) and the change request (C-020); confirm both resolve to a single successful approval each, with the second call in each case correctly detected as idempotent (returning existing state) rather than erroring unpredictably or, worse, creating duplicate customer/commercial/history records; per Pack D/E/F/G, confirm the same double-click safety holds for Commercial and Go Live approval actions, described here only as a consistency expectation.
- Stress Variant: Extend to 5+ rapid repeated clicks/calls across all four domains simultaneously.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This journey is closely related to, but distinct from, the multi-reviewer race conditions (A-031); here the SAME actor is the source of the duplicate calls, not two different reviewers.
- Idempotency Variant: This IS the idempotency journey, consolidated across all governed domains.
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Exactly one authoritative approval event per case/request across every domain tested, regardless of call repetition; no duplicated customer rows, commercial configurations, or field-history entries anywhere.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: The UI should ideally disable the Approve button immediately on first click to minimize the chance of this scenario in practice, though the server-side idempotency guarantee is the true safety net regardless of UI mitigation.
- UX Checks: Repeated clicks should feel like a harmless no-op from the user's perspective in every domain, with consistent messaging.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: A uniform, platform-wide guarantee that accidental duplicate approval attempts never corrupt business/financial truth, this is one of the most fundamental cross-cutting correctness properties the entire test catalogue protects.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Idempotent-on-approved-status behavior is confirmed explicitly for Onboarding (A-032) and Customer Change (C-020) in this pack's grounding; Commercial and Go Live's equivalent guarantee is expected but owned by Pack D/E/F/G's own testing.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL (Commercial/Go Live legs owned by Pack D/E/F/G)
- Dependencies: A-032, C-020
- Related Journeys: A-032, C-020, A-031
- Notes: N/A

- Regular Path: Approve a Customer Change moving the customer from Segment A to Segment B. Immediately afterward, create a new Commercial Configuration Version for that same customer. Confirm the new version's decision-node context reflects Segment B.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: The new version's workflow routing and its workflow_node_transitions history reflect Segment B, not the pre-change Segment A.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Commercial routing always reflects the current, approved Customer Master state at the moment a new version is created.
- Expected Technical Invariants: No caching of the customer's prior segment leaks into a newly created version's routing decision.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A

- Notes: Added during gap analysis. Distinct from E-010, which proves an already-created version does NOT retroactively re-route when segment changes later; this journey proves the positive forward path instead.

The existing AA-016-style proof uses two domains that both always take the default branch; this journey substitutes Commercial Configuration specifically because it is the only domain where routing genuinely depends on evaluated conditions, making cross-contamination a materially more meaningful risk to rule out.
## Pack AB: Security / Direct Action / Server Enforcement

### AB-001: Unauthenticated direct call to a Server Action is denied
- Pack: AB - Security / Direct Action / Server Enforcement
- Business Objective: Confirm no Server Action is reachable without any session at all, regardless of what the client sends.
- Domain: Cross-domain (Server Action layer)
- Object / Record Type: Any governed Server Action
- Starting State: No Supabase Auth cookie/session present at all.
- Personas: anonymous caller
- Preconditions: Ability to invoke a Server Action directly (e.g. via crafted request), bypassing normal UI navigation.
- Regular Path: Caller invokes a Server Action (e.g. an approve action) with no session cookie; requirePermission resolves the session as "unauthenticated" and throws AuthorizationError before any business logic or DB write executes.
- Stress Variant: Rapid repeated unauthenticated calls.
- Authorization Variant: This IS the authorization variant.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No row is written, no audit_log entry attributing an actor is created, since there is no real actor.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Zero data mutation is possible without authentication, no matter how the request is shaped.
- Expected Technical Invariants: requirePermission always runs before any mutation; the typed AuthorizationError names "unauthenticated" specifically.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: AB-002, AB-003, AB-004, AB-005
- Notes: N/A

### AB-011: Attempt to approve a request that has already been cancelled

### AB-013: Adversarial reuse of a stale expected_current_node_key to force an out-of-sequence transition
- Pack: AB - Security / Direct Action / Server Enforcement

- Domain: Workflow
- Object / Record Type: workflow request

- Preconditions: Caller intentionally, not accidentally, resubmits the stale key value.
- Regular Path: Caller deliberately calls the transition RPC/Server Action passing the stale node-A key while the request is actually at node B; the server compares the current actual node key against the supplied expected key, finds a mismatch, and rejects the call; the request's real current node (B) is unaffected.

- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No transition or approval is recorded from this call; the request's node history shows no anomalous entry.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: The workflow's sequencing cannot be manipulated by replaying an old client-side state, even deliberately.
- Expected Technical Invariants: expected_current_node_key is validated against live server state on every write, functioning as a genuine optimistic-lock/security control, not merely a UX nicety.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A

### AB-014: Tampered/spoofed actor field in a Server Action payload is ignored
- Pack: AB - Security / Direct Action / Server Enforcement
- Business Objective: Confirm the server never trusts a client-supplied user/actor identifier for authorization or audit attribution.
- Domain: Cross-domain
- Object / Record Type: Any mutating Server Action
- Starting State: Caller C is logged in as themselves but crafts a request payload containing a different user's id in any actor/user-id-shaped field the client happens to send.
- Personas: C (real identity), spoofed identity (a different, more privileged user)
- Preconditions: Ability to construct/modify the outgoing payload before it reaches the server.
- Regular Path: C submits the action with the tampered actor field claiming to be the more privileged user; the server ignores this field entirely, deriving identity solely from the server-side session (getCurrentNexusSession); the action is evaluated, permitted, and attributed strictly as C, using C's real permissions, not the spoofed identity's.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: This IS the authorization variant.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: audit_log.actor_user_id and any created_by/granted_by fields reflect C's real id, never the spoofed value; set_config('app.current_user_id', ...) is populated from the session, not the payload.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Client-supplied identity claims have zero effect on authorization or attribution.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Identity is derived exclusively server-side from the Auth session cookie, on every call, with no fallback to client-supplied fields.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: AB-015, N-028
- Notes: N/A

### AB-030: Permission removed in the narrow race window between page load and click completing (PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 3)
- Pack: AB - Security / Direct Action / Server Enforcement
- Business Objective: Confirm the permission check happens genuinely at the moment the server processes the request, closing any window where a click "in flight" during a revoke could sneak through.
- Domain: Cross-domain (any governed approval page)
- Object / Record Type: Any governed request
- Starting State: M has the approval page loaded and is in the act of clicking Approve at the exact moment an admin executes the revoke.
- Personas: user_access_admin (revokes at the precise moment), M (clicking)
- Preconditions: Requires timing the revoke to land as close as possible to the click's network request reaching the server (test harness should simulate this precisely, e.g. by pausing the request server-side, revoking, then resuming).
- Regular Path: The click's network request is deliberately delayed/paused server-side; the revoke is executed during the pause; the request is then allowed to resume and complete; requirePermission, evaluated at actual execution time (not at click time), correctly denies the action.
- Stress Variant: Repeated rapid clicks straddling the revoke instant.
- Authorization Variant: This IS the authorization variant, and the specific race case.
- Concurrency Variant: This IS the concurrency variant.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No approval row is created regardless of how narrow the race window is.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: There is no timing window, however narrow, in which a revoked permission still allows the action.
- Expected Technical Invariants: The permission check is evaluated strictly at request-processing time on the server, not cached from any earlier point (e.g. page load, click time).
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: O-015, AB-029, AB-036
- Notes: Directly corresponds to PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 3; requires deliberate server-side pausing in the test harness to reproduce reliably.

### AB-031: Permission restored after a revoke succeeds cleanly with no leftover error state (PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 4)

- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Exactly one successful action record is created, cleanly, post-restoration.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: This IS the recovery variant.
- UX Checks: Any earlier error messaging is fully cleared once the retried action succeeds.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Permission restoration is fully effective immediately, with a clean recovery path for the end user.
- Expected Technical Invariants: No caching or stale-negative-result persistence blocks the now-valid retry.
- Priority: P1
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: AB-028, AB-029, O-016
- Notes: Directly corresponds to PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 4.

### AB-032: Role revoked entirely mid-session denies the very next server action without requiring re-login (PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 7)
- Pack: AB - Security / Direct Action / Server Enforcement

- Regular Path: Admin revokes M's entire role (revoked_at set on the user_roles row) while M remains logged in with the same browser session; M attempts any action that depended on that role; requirePermission re-derives M's current roles fresh from the database on this call and denies with missing_permission, with no need for M to log out and back in for the denial to take effect.

- Authorization Variant: This IS the authorization variant.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No action succeeds using the revoked role's permissions after the revoke.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Role revocation is effective immediately, mid-session, proving there is no session-lifetime caching of roles.
- Expected Technical Invariants: The permission chain query (app_users -> user_roles -> roles -> role_permissions -> permissions) runs fresh on every requirePermission call, never once per session/login.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: N-009, AB-033
- Notes: Directly corresponds to PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 7.

### AB-036: Permission revoked while a Server Action call is already in flight (PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 14)
- Pack: AB - Security / Direct Action / Server Enforcement
- Business Objective: Directly verify there is no caching of the permission check: a request that left the browser before the revoke, but arrives at the server after it, must be denied.
- Domain: Cross-domain
- Object / Record Type: Any governed mutating Server Action
- Starting State: M initiates an action (the request leaves M's browser) at time T0, while M still holds the required permission.
- Personas: user_access_admin (revokes at T0.5, between send and server processing), M (whose in-flight request is affected)
- Preconditions: Test harness must be able to delay the request's arrival/processing at the server (e.g. artificial network delay or a server-side pause) so the revoke can be executed strictly between T0 (send) and T1 (server processing).
- Regular Path: M's request leaves the browser at T0 carrying no permission state of its own, only the session cookie; the admin revokes M's relevant permission at T0.5; the server processes the request at T1, calling requirePermission which reads the CURRENT (post-revoke) permission state fresh from the database; the action is correctly denied, proving requirePermission does not use any permission snapshot taken at request-send time.
- Stress Variant: Multiple in-flight requests from M straddling the revoke instant.
- Authorization Variant: This IS the authorization variant.
- Concurrency Variant: This IS the concurrency variant.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No mutation is recorded from this in-flight request.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: The permission check is truly per-request and real-time, with zero caching at any layer (browser, server process, or DB query result).
- Expected Technical Invariants: requirePermission performs a fresh database read of the full permission chain on every single invocation, never memoized within or across requests.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: AB-030, N-014
- Notes: Directly corresponds to PERMISSION-CHANGE scenario 14; requires a controllable delay in the test harness to land the revoke precisely mid-flight.

### AB-037: Permission granted while a Server Action call is already in flight (allow-path counterpart to scenario 14)
- Pack: AB - Security / Direct Action / Server Enforcement
- Business Objective: Confirm the fresh, no-caching permission check works symmetrically in the allow direction: a request sent before a grant, arriving after it, should succeed.
- Domain: Cross-domain
- Object / Record Type: Any governed mutating Server Action
- Starting State: M initiates an action at T0 that would normally be denied (M lacks the permission at T0).
- Personas: user_access_admin (grants at T0.5, between send and server processing), M (whose in-flight request benefits)
- Preconditions: Test harness must delay the request's arrival/processing so the grant lands strictly between send and server processing.
- Regular Path: M's request leaves the browser at T0 while M still lacks the permission; the admin grants M the permission at T0.5; the server processes the request at T1, and requirePermission reads the now-current (post-grant) state fresh, allowing the action to succeed even though M lacked the permission at the moment they clicked.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: This IS the authorization variant, the allow-path counterpart to AB-036.
- Concurrency Variant: This IS the concurrency variant.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: The resulting mutation is correctly attributed to M and correctly reflects that permission existed at processing time.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: The freshness guarantee cuts both ways: no stale-deny caching either, only true request-time evaluation.
- Expected Technical Invariants: Symmetric to AB-036: requirePermission has no directional bias or caching in either the deny or allow direction.
- Priority: P2
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: AB-036
- Notes: N/A

### AB-039: Concurrent approve attempts by two different eligible checkers on the same node
- Pack: AB - Security / Direct Action / Server Enforcement
- Business Objective: Confirm exactly one approval wins when two legitimately eligible checkers race to approve the same request, with the loser getting a clean, informative failure rather than a corrupted double-approval.
- Domain: Workflow
- Object / Record Type: workflow request
- Starting State: A request sits at an Approval node responsible to Team X; two different active Team X members, both holding valid checker permission, have the review page open simultaneously.
- Personas: checker 1, checker 2 (both eligible, same team)
- Preconditions: N/A
- Regular Path: Both checkers click Approve at nearly the same instant; the server processes both calls, but the expected_current_node_key / status check ensures only the first to actually commit succeeds in transitioning the request; the second call's expected_current_node_key no longer matches (the node has already moved), so it is rejected with a clear "already actioned" style error, not a duplicate approval.
- Stress Variant: More than two simultaneous checkers racing.
- Authorization Variant: N/A
- Concurrency Variant: This IS the concurrency variant.
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: Exactly one approval event exists in the audit trail; the request's node history shows a single, unambiguous transition.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: The losing checker sees an honest "someone else already actioned this" message, not a generic error or a false-success state.
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: Concurrent legitimate approvers never produce a corrupted or double-counted business outcome.
- Expected Technical Invariants: The same expected_current_node_key optimistic-concurrency mechanism used against adversarial reuse (AB-013) also correctly resolves honest, simultaneous races between two legitimate actors.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: PARTIAL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: AB-013, O-005
- Notes: N/A

### AB-040: Underlying Server Action invoked directly without ever rendering the AuthGate-wrapped page
- Pack: AB - Security / Direct Action / Server Enforcement
- Business Objective: Confirm the AuthGate check is not a prerequisite step baked into the action's own code path, i.e. skipping the page's render/mount lifecycle entirely still results in correct enforcement.
- Domain: Cross-domain
- Object / Record Type: Any governed Server Action bound to an AuthGate-wrapped route
- Starting State: A user lacking the route's required permission, who never once loads the route's page component in their browser.
- Personas: any under-permissioned user
- Preconditions: Ability to invoke the bound Server Action directly (e.g. via its known action id/endpoint) without first navigating to or rendering the page that would normally trigger AuthGate.
- Regular Path: Caller invokes the Server Action directly, having never triggered AuthGate's render-time check at all; requirePermission inside the Server Action itself still independently resolves the session and denies correctly, proving enforcement does not depend on AuthGate ever having run.
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: This IS the authorization variant.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: N/A
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No mutation occurs.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: N/A
- Expected Business Result: There is no code path in which skipping the page entirely grants any advantage to an attacker; the Server Action is self-contained in its enforcement.
- Expected Technical Invariants: AuthGate and requirePermission are fully independent checks; the Server Action never assumes AuthGate already ran.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: AB-006, AB-007
- Notes: This is the most direct, generalized statement of the pack's core thesis: a Server Action's own indirection is not authorization by itself, only requirePermission inside it is.

### AB-041: Governed backend-only RPC must not grant PostgreSQL execute privilege to anon/authenticated (new, discovered Batch 7 closure)
- Pack: AB - Security / Direct Action / Server Enforcement
- Business Objective: Every governed mutation RPC intended as backend-only (called exclusively via getSupabaseServiceRoleClient()) must be explicitly unreachable by the anon/authenticated Postgres roles at the database grant level, not merely "safe in practice" because some unrelated internal table happens to lack its own grant.
- Domain: Cross-domain (found across Customer Onboarding, Customer Change, Commercial Configuration, Customer Master, Go Live)
- Object / Record Type: pg_proc entries for any function matching a governed-mutation name pattern
- Starting State: A migration creates or replaces a governed mutation RPC and revokes execute from anon/authenticated by name, but never from PUBLIC, leaving Postgres's default PUBLIC execute grant in place (every role implicitly inherits PUBLIC's privileges, so naming anon/authenticated specifically does not remove it).
- Personas: Any authenticated Nexus user (any role, any permission set), tested via the public anon key with no session at all for the base case
- Preconditions: None; this is a database-privilege state, not an application-level condition.
- Regular Path: `select * from list_governed_rpc_grant_violations();` (migration 20260930070000_governed_rpc_revoke_public_execute_sweep.sql) returns zero rows; a raw PostgREST call to any governed backend-only RPC using only the public anon key returns `permission denied for function <name>` (SQLSTATE 42501).
- Stress Variant: N/A
- Authorization Variant: This IS the authorization variant.
- Concurrency Variant: N/A
- Idempotency Variant: Re-running the guard query after any future migration touching one of these functions must still return zero rows.
- Audit/Data Integrity Checks: No mutation occurs when correctly denied; no table is ever reached.
- Recovery/Resilience Variant: N/A
- UX Checks: N/A
- Historical Variant: 18 functions were found with this latent gap during Batch 7's post-completion closure investigation (4 Customer Onboarding functions fixed first via migration 20260930060000, then 14 more found and fixed via migration 20260930070000 after a name-prefix search proved incomplete and a full-schema `authenticated_execute = true` query was used instead); none had ever been actually exploited, since each happened to fail on a missing internal table grant first, but that was accidental, not intentional, protection.
- Expected Business Result: A new governed mutation RPC can never silently accumulate this exact gap again without the guard query surfacing it.
- Expected Technical Invariants: `list_governed_rpc_grant_violations()` (pattern-matches function names against a governed-mutation-verb regex, not a hardcoded list, specifically so a newly-added function is caught automatically) always returns zero rows in a healthy database state.
- Priority: P0
- Automation Feasibility: FULL
- Dependencies: N/A
- Related Journeys: AB-040
- Notes: Regression tooling: `scripts/verify-governed-rpc-grants.ts` (run via `npx tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/verify-governed-rpc-grants.ts`) calls the guard function and fails loudly on any violation. Recommended to run before applying any migration that creates, replaces, or changes the signature of a governed mutation RPC. See `docs/journey-runs/BATCH_07_RESULTS.md` (DEFECT-B7-003) for the full discovery and fix narrative.

## FUTURE Journey Packs

The following two packs are explicitly excluded from the current executable count (773 journeys above). Neither module exists in the Nexus product today; these are high-level planned-coverage placeholders only, in the lighter-weight format described in each pack's own framing paragraph, not executable test journeys.

## FUTURE JOURNEY PACK: Forms Hub

Forms Hub does not exist in the current product. Today, finding work is entirely list/table/link based across four separate surfaces (My Work, Approvals, Operational Queue, Customer Master search), with no unified inbox, no global search, and no "all forms for a customer" or "all submissions of a form type" view anywhere in the codebase. The journeys below are planned-coverage placeholders describing what a future Forms Hub would need to prove out; they are not executable test journeys and should not be treated as current coverage.

### FH-001: Unified inbox surfaces all four governed request types
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Verify a single hub view can list Customer Onboarding, Customer Change, Commercial Configuration Version, and Go Live items without dropping or duplicating any of them.
- Depends On (not yet built): A unified data model or aggregation layer spanning the four existing request tables/workflows.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Cross-domain data consistency
- Notes: Today each type lives in its own table with its own status enum; naive UNION queries risk column/semantic mismatches (e.g. "pending" meaning different things per type).

### FH-002: All-forms-for-customer view
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Confirm a user can pull up every request of every type ever submitted for a given customer, replacing manual cross-referencing.
- Depends On (not yet built): A customer-scoped join across all request tables keyed consistently to customer identity.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Cross-domain data consistency
- Notes: Must account for customer renames/merges (customer_field_history) so historical forms under an old name still surface.

### FH-003: Cross-domain "all Legal-pending" query
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Verify a Legal reviewer can see every open item awaiting Legal action across all form types and workflow nodes in one query.
- Depends On (not yet built): A normalized workflow-node/approver-role model that is queryable independent of form type.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Cross-domain data consistency
- Notes: Today "pending Legal" is implicit in per-type workflow state; there is no shared vocabulary for workflow node across types yet.

### FH-004: Global full-text/fuzzy search replaces exact-match query params
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Confirm free-text search returns relevant results despite typos, partial names, or reordered words, unlike today's exact/substring param search.
- Depends On (not yet built): A full-text or fuzzy search index (e.g. trigram/pg_trgm or external search service) over form and customer content.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Search relevance / correctness
- Notes: Should validate ranking quality, not just recall, once built.

### FH-005: Search respects per-type authorization
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Verify a user without access to a given request type never sees its records surface in unified search or hub results.
- Depends On (not yet built): Hub-level enforcement of existing per-type RBAC rules at query time.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Authorization
- Notes: High-risk area; a hub that aggregates across tables is an easy place to accidentally bypass existing row-level access checks.

### FH-006: Hub badge/count parity with My Work and Approvals
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Confirm counts and badges shown in the new hub match the existing My Work and Approvals counts exactly, with no drift or double-counting.
- Depends On (not yet built): Shared counting logic or a single source of truth reused by both old and new surfaces.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Cross-domain data consistency
- Notes: Risk of two divergent implementations of "what counts as pending for me" living side by side.

### FH-007: Deep link from hub result into the correct type-specific detail view
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Verify clicking a hub search result routes to the exact existing detail/edit screen for that request type and record.
- Depends On (not yet built): A stable, type-aware routing scheme keyed off hub result records.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Functional correctness
- Notes: Each of the four types currently has its own detail route; hub must not attempt to render a generic view that loses type-specific fields.

### FH-008: Saved searches / saved views per user
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Confirm a user can save a filtered cross-type view (e.g. "my open Go Lives + Commercial Configs") and reload it later with fresh data.
- Depends On (not yet built): Persistence layer for saved filter definitions scoped to user/team.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Functional correctness
- Notes: Should verify saved views re-execute live (not snapshot stale data) on reload.

### FH-009: Team-shared saved views
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Verify a saved view can be shared with a team and all members see consistent, permission-filtered results.
- Depends On (not yet built): Saved-view sharing plus per-viewer permission re-evaluation at render time.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Authorization
- Notes: A shared view must not leak records to a teammate who lacks access to the underlying request type.

### FH-010: Aging / SLA view across all request types
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Confirm the hub can show "oldest open items across all types" to help surface stuck workflows regardless of which type they belong to.
- Depends On (not yet built): A normalized "age since last action" metric computed consistently across differently-shaped workflow tables.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial/operational correctness (SLA breach visibility)
- Notes: Each type may define "last action" differently today; must reconcile before a single aging metric is meaningful.

### FH-011: Bulk actions across mixed-type result sets
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Verify selecting multiple hub results of different types and applying a bulk action (e.g. reassign, remind) applies correctly per type.
- Depends On (not yet built): Type-aware bulk-action dispatch that respects each type's own workflow rules.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Functional correctness
- Notes: A generic bulk action must not apply a state transition that is invalid for a given type's workflow.

### FH-012: Hub reflects real-time status changes made outside the hub
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Confirm an approval or edit made via the existing per-type screens (not the hub) is reflected in hub views without stale caching.
- Depends On (not yet built): Cache invalidation or live-query strategy tying hub views to underlying source tables.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Cross-domain data consistency
- Notes: Two entry points (old screens + new hub) writing/reading the same underlying data is a classic source of stale-read bugs.

### FH-013: Drafts-to-continue coverage inside the hub
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Verify in-progress drafts across all four types are discoverable from the hub, matching today's "Drafts to Continue" section in My Work.
- Depends On (not yet built): Draft-state records included in the hub's unified query, with correct owner scoping.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Functional correctness
- Notes: Drafts are inherently private to their author; hub aggregation must not expose other users' drafts.

### FH-014: Former-name customer search integrated into hub
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Confirm the existing genuine former-name search (via customer_field_history) is preserved and surfaced through the new hub search rather than regressed.
- Depends On (not yet built): Hub search indexing that includes historical name variants, not just current customer name.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Regression / functional correctness
- Notes: This is one of the few genuinely real search capabilities today; it must not be quietly dropped when the hub replaces ad hoc search entry points.

### FH-015: Pagination and sort stability under concurrent updates
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Verify large cross-type result sets paginate correctly and don't skip/duplicate rows when underlying records change between page loads.
- Depends On (not yet built): A stable sort/cursor strategy for a query spanning multiple heterogeneous tables.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Performance / correctness at scale
- Notes: Union-based queries across tables with different indexing strategies are prone to inconsistent pagination.

### FH-016: Performance at scale for large customer portfolios
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Confirm hub queries remain responsive when a customer or user has hundreds/thousands of associated forms across all types.
- Depends On (not yet built): Indexing/query plan validated against realistic production-scale data volumes.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Performance
- Notes: No current single-customer aggregation exists to benchmark against; this is a net-new performance surface.

### FH-017: Empty and zero-result states across combined filters
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Verify the hub handles legitimate "nothing matches" cases (e.g. a Legal-pending filter for a customer with no forms) without misleading messaging or errors.
- Depends On (not yet built): Defined empty-state UX for cross-domain filtered queries.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Functional correctness
- Notes: Low complexity but easy to overlook; combined filters multiply the number of empty-state paths to cover.

### FH-018: Export of cross-type hub results
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Confirm a filtered, cross-type hub result set can be exported (e.g. CSV) with fields correctly mapped per source type.
- Depends On (not yet built): A unified export schema that can represent heterogeneous form-type fields sensibly.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Data correctness
- Notes: Naive flattening risks blank/misaligned columns when exporting mixed record shapes.

### FH-019: Notification/alert consistency with hub-surfaced items
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Verify notifications a user receives about pending work correspond exactly to what the hub shows as pending for them, with no orphaned notifications.
- Depends On (not yet built): Shared eventing/notification source feeding both hub state and notification delivery.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Cross-domain data consistency
- Notes: Risk of a notification pointing to a record the hub no longer considers "pending" due to a race condition.

### FH-020: Access-control regression check when new request types are added later
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Confirm that adding a fifth (future) governed request type to the hub does not require rewriting authorization logic per existing type, and doesn't accidentally widen access.
- Depends On (not yet built): An extensible, type-agnostic authorization model for the hub itself.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Authorization
- Notes: Forward-looking check; hub design choices made now will determine how safely new request types can be onboarded later.

### FH-021: Mobile/responsive parity for hub search and filters
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Verify the hub's cross-type search and filter UI remains usable on smaller viewports, since existing per-type list views are desktop-oriented today.
- Depends On (not yet built): Responsive hub UI design and layout.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Functional correctness
- Notes: Lower priority than data-correctness items but worth flagging early given four existing surfaces are desktop-first.

### FH-022: Audit trail consolidation across form types
- Pack: FH
- Business Objective: Confirm the hub can present a unified audit/history timeline for a customer or record spanning multiple request types, not just per-type history.
- Depends On (not yet built): A normalized audit-event schema shared across all governed request types.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Cross-domain data consistency
- Notes: Each type likely logs history differently today; reconciling into one timeline view is nontrivial.


## FUTURE JOURNEY PACK: MRR Recognition

MRR Recognition does not exist in the current product. Only its integration boundary is present today, a single recognition_status placeholder field; the actual monthly recurring revenue computation, recognition schedules, and posting/reversal logic have not been built. The journeys below describe planned coverage that would build on the real, already-implemented Entitlement Ledger and Commercial Configuration/Component pricing models; they are placeholders for future test design, not currently runnable journeys.

### MRR-001: Recognition schedule generation from entitlement sources
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Verify a recognition schedule can be derived correctly from entitlement_sources and entitlement_schedule_months for a standard recurring component.
- Depends On (not yet built): The recognition schedule engine itself; today entitlement_schedule_months exists for billing/entitlement purposes only, not recognition.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: Must clarify whether recognition timing is meant to mirror entitlement timing or diverge (e.g. ratably vs point-in-time).

### MRR-002: Straight-line recognition for flat pricing components
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Confirm flat-priced components recognize revenue evenly across the contracted period.
- Depends On (not yet built): Recognition posting logic keyed to the existing flat pricing rule kind.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: Simplest case; good baseline before tackling volume/graduated/dimension pricing recognition.

### MRR-003: Usage-based recognition for linear/volume pricing components
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Verify components priced with linear or volume pricing rules recognize revenue based on actual monthly_usage rather than a flat schedule.
- Depends On (not yet built): Recognition logic that consumes monthly_usage records as its computation input.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: Needs to handle usage reported late or corrected after the recognition period closes.

### MRR-004: Recognition for graduated/tiered pricing components
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Confirm graduated pricing rules recognize the correct blended amount per tier rather than a single flat rate.
- Depends On (not yet built): Tier-aware recognition computation reusing the existing graduated pricing rule definitions.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: Edge cases at tier boundaries mid-period will need explicit coverage once buildable.

### MRR-005: Recognition for dimension-based pricing components
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Verify components priced via dimension pricing rules recognize revenue correctly when the dimension value changes mid-period.
- Depends On (not yet built): Dimension-aware recognition logic and a defined proration rule for dimension changes.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: Highest-complexity pricing kind; likely last to be built and tested in practice.

### MRR-006: MUG quantity floor impact on recognized revenue
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Confirm that when a Minimum Usage Guarantee floor is applied, recognized revenue reflects the floor amount rather than actual (lower) usage.
- Depends On (not yet built): Recognition logic that reads the MUG floor outcome from the entitlement/billing layer as its recognition basis.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: Must verify the floor "topped-up" portion is recognized consistently with how it is billed, to avoid revenue/billing mismatches.

### MRR-007: Non-recurring revenue posts an actual journal entry
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Verify that selecting a non-recurring revenue recognition method actually results in a posted journal entry, closing today's gap where only the method choice is captured.
- Depends On (not yet built): Journal-entry posting logic triggered by the existing non-recurring revenue recognition method field.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: This is explicitly called out as a known gap today (method captured, nothing posted); a priority journey once buildable.

### MRR-008: recognition_status state machine transitions
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Confirm the recognition_status field transitions correctly (e.g. scheduled, recognized, reversed) as recognition events occur.
- Depends On (not yet built): A defined state machine and the events that drive its transitions.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: Since this field already exists as a placeholder, its allowed values/transitions should be defined before schedule logic is built on top of it.

### MRR-009: Recognition reversal on contract cancellation
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Verify that canceling a contract or component mid-period correctly reverses any future-scheduled but not-yet-recognized revenue.
- Depends On (not yet built): Reversal logic tied to cancellation events and recognition_status transitions.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: Must distinguish reversing unrecognized future amounts from clawing back already-recognized amounts (likely requires a credit memo path instead).

### MRR-010: Proration on mid-month commercial configuration changes
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Confirm a mid-month change to a Commercial Configuration Version prorates recognized revenue correctly between the old and new configuration.
- Depends On (not yet built): Recognition-aware proration logic reacting to Commercial Configuration Version changes.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: Needs tight coordination with the existing versioning model for Commercial Configuration so recognition doesn't double count or drop the transition month.

### MRR-011: Reconciliation between recognized revenue and unbilled_ledger_entries
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Verify recognized revenue ties out against unbilled_ledger_entries so recognition never gets ahead of or behind what has actually been entitled/billed.
- Depends On (not yet built): A reconciliation report or check comparing recognition totals against the existing unbilled ledger.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Cross-domain data consistency
- Notes: This is the core "does recognition agree with the real ledger" check; high value once both sides exist.

### MRR-012: Reconciliation between recognized revenue and unearned_ledger_entries
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Confirm the deferred/unearned balance decreases correctly as amounts are recognized, keeping unearned_ledger_entries and recognition in sync.
- Depends On (not yet built): Recognition logic that reads and updates unearned ledger balances as part of posting.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: A mismatch here would represent a real deferred-revenue accounting error, the highest-severity class of bug for this pack.

### MRR-013: Settlement record tie-out after recognition
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Verify settlement_records remain consistent with recognized revenue amounts after a settlement event touches a component with an active recognition schedule.
- Depends On (not yet built): Defined interaction between settlement processing and recognition schedule updates.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Cross-domain data consistency
- Notes: Order-of-operations matters: does settlement trigger recognition, or does recognition run independently and settlement merely reads its output.

### MRR-014: Backdated entitlement change triggers recognition recalculation
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Confirm that a backdated correction to an entitlement source correctly recalculates and adjusts already-posted recognition for affected prior periods.
- Depends On (not yet built): Recalculation/adjustment logic capable of amending closed recognition periods.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: Needs a clear policy on whether prior-period recognition can be reopened or whether adjustments always land in the current period.

### MRR-015: Period close lock prevents further recognition changes
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Verify that once a recognition period is closed, no further postings or edits are possible against that period, protecting closed-period financial integrity.
- Depends On (not yet built): A period-close/lock mechanism for recognition, analogous to standard accounting period close.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness / authorization
- Notes: Should also verify who is authorized to reopen a closed period, since that is a high-risk override.

### MRR-016: Authorization for posting and reversing recognition entries
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Confirm only appropriately privileged roles can post or reverse recognition journal entries.
- Depends On (not yet built): Role/permission model specific to recognition actions, separate from existing Commercial Configuration approval roles.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Authorization
- Notes: Recognition posting is a financial-statement-impacting action and likely needs its own approval workflow, not reuse of existing configuration approvals.

### MRR-017: Multi-currency recognition consistency
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Verify recognized revenue amounts are computed and reported in the correct currency, consistent with the underlying entitlement and billing currency.
- Depends On (not yet built): Currency handling within the recognition engine, and a defined FX policy if reporting currency differs from contract currency.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: Needs to confirm whether recognition ever requires FX conversion or always stays in contract currency.

### MRR-018: Recognition dashboard/report accuracy at scale
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Confirm a recognition summary report (e.g. total MRR recognized this period) matches the sum of underlying schedule entries exactly, even at high record volumes.
- Depends On (not yet built): A recognition reporting layer and defined aggregation rules.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Performance / financial correctness
- Notes: Should include a check that report totals recompute correctly after any mid-period adjustment or reversal.

### MRR-019: Amendment to Commercial Configuration Version mid-recognition-period
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Verify an approved amendment to a Commercial Configuration Version part-way through a recognition period correctly splits recognition between old and new terms.
- Depends On (not yet built): Recognition awareness of Commercial Configuration Version history/effective-dating.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Cross-domain data consistency
- Notes: Closely related to MRR-010 but focused on the versioning/audit trail angle rather than pure proration math.

### MRR-020: Restatement/correction workflow for prior-period recognition errors
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Confirm a discovered recognition error from a prior closed period can be corrected through an auditable restatement rather than a silent edit.
- Depends On (not yet built): A restatement workflow with its own audit trail, distinct from normal reversal handling.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness / auditability
- Notes: Should verify the original erroneous entries remain visible in history rather than being overwritten, for audit purposes.

### MRR-021: Recognition correctness under contract churn mid-cycle
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Verify that a customer churning mid-cycle results in correct partial-period recognition and correct treatment of any remaining deferred balance.
- Depends On (not yet built): Churn-event handling wired into the recognition and unearned-ledger reconciliation logic.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Financial correctness
- Notes: Overlaps with MRR-009 (cancellation reversal) but specifically targets the deferred-balance disposition question (refund vs forfeiture vs write-off).

### MRR-022: Performance of recognition batch runs at high customer/component volume
- Pack: MRR
- Business Objective: Confirm month-end recognition batch processing completes within an acceptable window when run across a large portfolio of customers and components.
- Depends On (not yet built): The batch recognition job itself and realistic production-scale test data.
- Anticipated Risk Category: Performance
- Notes: No current equivalent batch process exists to benchmark against; this is entirely new operational surface once built.
