## Gap Analysis Addendum

After the initial 773-journey catalogue was assembled, one adversarial gap-analysis pass was run against it (per the mission's required "what could a user do that has no journey, what state transition, permission mutation, concurrency race, recovery scenario, approved-truth invariant, and cross-domain linkage is not represented" questions), reading the assembled document and re-verifying claims directly against the live codebase rather than trusting prior summaries. It found the catalogue's coverage was already unusually thorough; nine concrete, code-verified gaps survived scrutiny and were added directly into their relevant packs: H-043, I-038, K-029, N-031, S-024, Z-030, ACC-001 (a new, intentionally small Accessibility pack), AA-021, and AA-022. No further gap-analysis round was run after these additions, since the surviving gap rate from the first pass was already low (9 out of 773) and the remaining candidate gaps raised during that pass were judged too speculative to catalogue as concrete journeys.

Two of the nine additions surfaced genuine current product findings, not merely absent tests, and both were independently confirmed by direct code/migration inspection during the 2026-09-16 reconciliation pass (see the "Reconciled 2026-09-16" notes on each journey for detail):
- N-031: CONFIRMED. `usage.read` and `entitlement_settlement.read` are seeded, real permission strings with zero `requirePermission`/`hasPermission` call sites anywhere in the codebase; the entitlement/usage/settlement page gates entry solely on `entitlement.read`. An admin who grants only one of these two narrow permissions is granting something that currently does nothing.
- H-043: CONFIRMED, with a narrower blast radius than first suspected. `go_live_requests` genuinely lacks the protect-trigger pattern used by Customer Master and Commercial Components (verified via direct migration inspection: only `updated_at`, audit, and row_version triggers exist on this table). However, RLS is enabled on the table with no policies, which already blocks the anon/authenticated roles a normal user or compromised client session could reach; the missing trigger only matters against a direct service_role or superuser database connection, a materially narrower threat than a UI/API-reachable bypass. Downgraded from P0 to P1 accordingly.

## Consolidated Product Gap Notes

Each authoring pass flagged what it found to be genuinely unbuilt, undocumented, or ambiguous while grounding its packs in the actual codebase. Consolidated here rather than scattered mid-document.

**Source: Packs A, B, C, AA (Customer Lifecycle)**

### PRODUCT GAP NOTES

The following are documented, code-confirmed gaps (not speculative bugs) surfaced while designing these journeys, each already called out inline in its relevant journey's Notes field:

1. Onboarding has no genuine terminal "rejected" state for a submitted case a reviewer never wants to approve; once submitted, a case can only be sent back indefinitely or approved, with cancellation restricted to draft-only. See A-020, AA-008.
2. WORKFLOW_TEAM_REQUIRED has no handling anywhere in the code when a workflow node's responsible team has zero active members; every approver attempt fails forever until an admin manually fixes team membership or the graph, with no automated recovery or cross-domain alerting. See A-027, C-025, AA-010.
3. Deactivating a customer blocks new Customer Change Request creation (B-010) but does NOT block creating a new Commercial Version against the same inactive customer (B-011), a confirmed, documented inconsistency with real business risk. See B-011, AA-011.
4. RECONCILED 2026-09-16, no longer an open gap: row-version optimistic locking across the four governed draft surfaces is now consistent platform-wide. Migration `20260922000000_optimistic_locking_extension.sql` extended the same `p_expected_row_version` staleness check already proven for `save_customer_change_draft` to `save_customer_onboarding_draft`, `save_commercial_configuration_version_draft`, `save_go_live_request_draft` (which also gained the `row_version` column it previously lacked entirely), and `save_workflow_version_graph`. Confirmed applied via the live Supabase migration ledger, not merely written to a file. A-030, E-013, K-010, V-001, V-011 through V-015, and AA-014 are now regression journeys proving this fix, not open-gap verifications.
5. Customer Change's own workflow-derived requirements (Segment/FINANCE_HEAD, Business Unit/BU_HEAD, Legal Entity Name/company_registration) are informational/transparency-only in V1, never a real per-requirement sign-off gate; this is a deliberate simplification worth flagging if the business later expects enforced multi-party sign-off. See C-007, C-011.
6. Legal Entity Name changes in Customer Change surface a company_registration evidence requirement, but Customer Change has no attachment/document-upload capability at all, unlike Onboarding and Go Live, so this requirement can never actually be satisfied with an uploaded document inside the product. See C-009, C-028, C-031.
7. Suspected but unverified gap: duplicate GST/PAN detection is explicitly scoped in the grounding brief to Onboarding, at Submit only; no equivalent duplicate check is described for Customer Change approval, potentially allowing a Customer Change to give one customer the same GST/PAN as another, unrelated, existing customer. This needs direct code verification before being treated as confirmed. See AA-015.
8. Whether renaming or archiving a Workflow Builder team retroactively affects the display of historical approval timelines (which live-resolve actor/team labels rather than using a write-time snapshot, except for Customer Master's own field history) is not fully specified in the grounding brief and should be verified directly; if team labels do live-update in historical timelines, it may create a misleading audit picture. See AA-005, AA-013.
9. Whether a unified, cross-domain customer activity/audit view exists (merging onboarding, change, deactivation/reactivation, and commercial/go-live events into one coherent timeline) is not confirmed in the grounding brief; if absent, auditors must currently assemble a full customer lifecycle picture manually across multiple separate domain screens. See AA-017.
10. Whether customer deactivation should, as a matter of business policy, cascade any review/suspension signal to already-live Commercial Configuration/Go Live records is an open question; today there is confirmed no such cascade, which may be correct by design or may be an unaddressed policy gap. See AA-018.


**Source: Packs D, E, F, G (Commercial)**

### PRODUCT GAP NOTES

- Package/block pricing: explicitly documented as deferred/future, not implemented anywhere in the current pricing_rule_kind check constraint or UI. No current-product journeys were written against it (see F-012). Future test-journey work should only begin once this is actually implemented.
- Wallet/prepaid balance pricing: same status as Package/block pricing, explicitly deferred/future, not implemented (see F-012). No current-product journeys written.
- Old ungoverned RPC create_commercial_change_for_configuration (D-017, E-020): a real, currently-existing "immediately live, no review" mutation path for commercial terms that coexists alongside the fully governed commercial_configuration_versions draft/submit/approve cycle. This is a genuine, present-day risk area (an unreviewed financial-truth mutation surface sitting next to a reviewed one) and should be prioritized for either retirement or governance, not merely tested around.
- RECONCILED 2026-09-16, no longer an open gap: row-version optimistic locking on commercial_configuration_versions (E-013) is now wired via `save_commercial_configuration_version_draft`'s `p_expected_row_version` check, confirmed applied to the live database (migration `20260922000000_optimistic_locking_extension.sql`). E-013 is now a regression journey, not an open-risk finding.
- No attachment/document support for Commercial Configuration or Commercial Change (D-018): confirmed zero matches in code for any file/document upload capability against these domains, a plausible expectation gap for finance teams wanting to attach signed contracts or addenda.
- Commercial "nature" (recurring / non_recurring / on_demand) is not a proper DB column (F-007): it lives only in the TypeScript layer and inside pricing_rule_parameters JSON. The DB's is_recurring boolean alone cannot distinguish non_recurring from on_demand components. Any BI/reporting tool or data pipeline built directly against the raw DB schema (bypassing the application layer) will misclassify or fail to distinguish these two natures. This is an honestly acknowledged schema gap, not a defect to silently work around; flagged here for whoever owns direct-DB reporting.
- Non-Recurring Revenue Recognition method (full_recognition / milestone_based) captured at the draft/version layer never posts any journal entry or feeds a real revenue-recognition engine (E-019); that engine is explicitly future/out of scope. Ensure UI copy does not overstate what this field actually does today, to avoid misleading finance users into thinking real revenue recognition is occurring.
- Component uniqueness is deliberately unenforced at the DB level (D-006, D-019): multiple simultaneous open components can exist for the same capability scope with no exclusion constraint. This is by design per the grounding brief, but it is also a genuine reviewer-visibility risk for accidental duplicate entry; consider a soft warning in the review UI even though the schema will not block it.
- MUG applicability boundaries for Designation Based components and for Non-Recurring components (G-017, G-022) were not explicitly confirmed either way in the grounding brief; these were flagged as open verification items for execution rather than assumed, and any surprising findings (e.g. a semantically meaningless MUG field being offered where it shouldn't be) should be escalated as product-risk items.
- Duplicate designation rows within a single dimension component (G-021): whether the UI even allows this and what the billing engine does if it is reachable is unverified in the grounding brief; flagged as a real ambiguity risk pending execution findings.


**Source: Packs H, I (Go Live / Entitlement)**

### PRODUCT GAP NOTES

- RECONCILED 2026-09-16: H-005's row-version optimistic lock on go_live_requests (save_go_live_request_draft's p_expected_row_version) is confirmed applied to the live database via the Supabase migration ledger (migration `20260922000000_optimistic_locking_extension.sql`, which also added the row_version column itself, since go_live_requests previously had none). H-005's protection is confirmed, not unverified.
- I-006: The grounding brief confirms allocation anchors to the go-live month but does not explicitly state whether generate_allocation_schedule can even be invoked before a Go Live request is approved (blocked vs. provisional generation). This needs direct verification against the actual RPC rather than assumption.
- I-016: Whether cancel_entitlement_source carries any self-action/creator restriction analogous to the go_live cancel/approve family is not explicitly confirmed in the grounding brief for this specific RPC (it has no obvious workflow-approver concept). Needs direct verification.
- I-034: No uniqueness constraint on entitlement_sources.invoiceReference is confirmed in the grounding brief; duplicate-invoice handling behavior is unverified and could be a genuine data-integrity gap if no constraint or warning exists.
- I-035: No confirmation exists that entitlement_sources.metric is validated against the referenced commercial component's actual billed metric; a mismatch could silently produce a meaningless ledger comparison. Recommend product/engineering confirm whether this validation exists.
- I-032: The coexistence of the legacy Commercial "Usage Fact/Earned Result" concept and the current Entitlement Ledger is a naming/mental-model confusion risk worth product attention even though the two are structurally unrelated; consider renaming or clearly labeling the legacy concept in any UI surface where both terms could appear near each other.
- H-032: Whether multiple simultaneous draft go_live_requests rows are permitted for the same line item (versus being constrained to one at a time) is not explicitly confirmed in the grounding brief; if unconstrained, this could allow analyst confusion about which draft is "the" active one.

**Source: Packs J, K, L, M (Workflow)**

### PRODUCT GAP NOTES

1. Team-with-zero-active-members (J-011, M-025) and team-deactivation-does-not-block-members (J-012, M-026) are both confirmed real, currently unhandled behaviors per the grounding brief; they are catalogued here as testable journeys, not proposed fixes, but both represent genuine operational risk (silent permanent orphaning; a misleading admin control) worth product attention.
2. The canApprove cross-domain OR-imprecision (M-020, M-021) creates at least a cosmetic list-level leak, and its actual severity (cosmetic-only vs a true RPC-level authorization gap) is explicitly flagged in M-021 as needing empirical confirmation rather than assumption; this is the single highest-value journey to run first in Pack M.
3. Save Draft Graph's whole-graph-replace mechanic (K-010) creates a genuine, currently real silent data-loss risk for concurrent Builder editors with no merge, warning, or content-level optimistic lock; row_version (L-015) protects the version row's lifecycle state but not the graph content itself.
4. A published graph with a validation gap (e.g. an Approval node with no outgoing edge) combined with the permanent workflow_version_id binding at request-creation time (J-015) can produce a request that is genuinely unrecoverable through any graph fix, since in-flight requests never rebind to a corrected version; this combination is worth product attention as it may warrant either stronger publish-time reachability/dead-end validation or an admin override to rebind a stuck in-flight request.
5. Decision nodes authored in customer_onboarding, customer_change, or go_live domains are effectively inert or actively dangerous today (J-007 through J-009, J-024) since those domains never populate a non-empty decision context; the Builder gives no warning when an admin adds a Decision node in these domains, making WORKFLOW_DECISION_NO_MATCH-driven total outages (J-024) a real, unguarded authoring risk.
6. Several Builder structural-edge-case outcomes (unreachable nodes at K-019, dangling edge references at K-020, duplicate node keys at K-021, End-node-with-outgoing-edge and Start-node-with-incoming-edge at K-025/K-026, and the minimum-viable-graph publish requirement at L-026) are catalogued as journeys whose expected outcome must be empirically confirmed against actual code, since the grounding brief does not explicitly assert behavior for these specific structural edge cases; none of these invent new mechanics, they probe the boundaries of documented ones.
7. The self-created-and-self-approvable item is correctly classified as "pending my approval" by list ordering (M-011) even though the RPC layer separately blocks actual self-approval; this produces a confirmed, real UX moment where the list tells the user an item is actionable but the action then fails, worth a clearer inline explanation rather than a generic RPC rejection message.

**Source: Packs N, O, AB (Identity / Security)**

### PRODUCT GAP NOTES

Authorization coverage in Nexus is explicitly, deliberately partial today, and this is disclosed rather than hidden: only Reference Master, Commercial Configuration, Customer lifecycle, User Access, Team, Workflow, Go Live, and Entitlement have requirePermission enforcement wired in as of this catalogue. Every other route or Server Action is documented as still unauthenticated-reachable, "to be closed feature by feature." AB-022 exists specifically to re-confirm this exposure surface honestly against current code each time this catalogue is exercised, rather than assuming full coverage exists; a route that AB-022 finds newly closed is progress, and a route expected to already be closed but found still open is a real regression worth escalating immediately.

Beyond that disclosed gap, three other real, confirmed-in-code behaviors are catalogued here as testable facts, not as newly discovered defects, per the grounding brief:
1. user_access.write can grant ANY role, including to oneself, with zero restriction (N-013, AB-021). This is the single largest concentration of trust in the system and is intentional, disclosed behavior.
2. Deactivating a team (teams.is_active = false) does not block its existing, still-unrevoked members from approving in-flight requests at that team's workflow nodes, because fn_require_workflow_team_membership checks only user_teams.revoked_at, never teams.is_active (O-005). Only individually revoking a person's own membership stops them.
3. Removing the last remaining active member of a team while a request sits at that team's node leaves the request permanently stuck with no automatic reassignment, alert, or escalation, until an admin manually intervenes (O-018).

Two smaller, narrower open questions are flagged for verification against current code rather than assumed either way: whether grant_user_role itself (not just the UI) rejects granting a deactivated role (AB-023, N-030), and the exact mechanism/RPC name behind reference_master's self-approval-style two-person control given that its listed permission strings are only read/write with no separate approve permission (AB-020).

**Source: Packs P, Q, R, S, T, U (Platform / Data)**

### PRODUCT GAP NOTES

The following are confirmed, real gaps in the current product, per the grounding brief. They are recorded here explicitly so reviewers do not mistake the corresponding verification journeys above for failed tests, and so a separate, higher-level FUTURE-capability pack can reference them without re-deriving the same findings.

- No shared attachments/documents module exists platform-wide. The attachment implementation is duplicated in exactly two places (Customer Onboarding's own implementation, and Go Live which reuses Onboarding's file-validation policy). Customer Change and Commercial Configuration/Version have zero attachment support today. See Q-013, Q-014.
- No global/omnibox search exists anywhere in the product outside the one real, narrowly-scoped Customer Master search (/customers with ?q=, ?segment=, ?businessUnit=, ?country=, ?status=, plus former-name search). The app shell nav itself has no search box at all. See S-023.
- No Forms Hub exists: there is no customer-to-all-forms view, no form-type-to-all-submissions view, no cross-form-type search-by-customer, and no cross-form-type "Pending Legal" (or any other role-scoped, cross-domain) discovery view. These are all desired-but-nonexistent capabilities; cross-reference the separate FUTURE Forms Hub pack another agent is writing at a higher level. See S-019, S-020, S-021, S-022.
- No team-lead concept exists in Team Master; membership is flat, with no elevated role or ownership designation for any team member. See T-022.
- Customer Master itself has no own rendered Timeline; only its onboarding case and change requests have one, plus a separate former-name/field-history mechanism unrelated to RequestTimeline. See R-013.
- Settings, Team Master, User Access, and Workflow Builder have no rendered Timeline UI at all; their history exists only in the raw, low-level audit_log table, never surfaced as a readable business Timeline in the product. See R-014.
- Team Master has no edit name/description control and no hard-delete control for teams; teams can only be created and activated/deactivated. See T-020, T-021 (and R-008, which notes the "team renamed after acting" scenario from the brief cannot actually be exercised today because no rename control exists).
- A known, confirmed real inconsistency: deactivating a TEAM does not block its still-assigned members from approving at a workflow node bound to that team; only revoking a member's own user_teams grant does, since the workflow-approval eligibility check reads only user_teams.revoked_at and never teams.is_active. See T-019.
- A suspected (not yet confirmed live) regression: the login page's post-sign-in redirect appears to always router.push("/my-work") without reading the redirectTo query param that AuthGate itself sets when bouncing an unauthenticated user off a deep link, contradicting an existing manual test item that claims the deep link is honored after sign-in. See U-005, explicitly framed as a verify-not-assume journey, Priority P2.

**Source: Packs V, W, X, Y, Z (Cross-cutting)**

### PRODUCT GAP NOTES

- RECONCILED 2026-09-16, no longer an open gap: the migration wiring row_version-based optimistic concurrency for Customer Onboarding drafts, Commercial Configuration Version drafts, Go Live drafts, and the Workflow Builder's own draft graph save (`20260922000000_optimistic_locking_extension.sql`) is confirmed applied via the live Supabase migration ledger. All five draft-editing surfaces (Customer Change already had its own equivalent fix first) now reject a stale concurrent save with a named `*_DRAFT_STALE` error rather than silently overwriting. V-001, V-011 through V-015, A-030, E-013, K-010, and AA-014 are regression journeys proving this, not open-gap verifications.
- No team-rename control exists: Team management currently has no free-text rename capability for workflow teams (see V-035). This should be verified against the live product on each catalogue refresh in case a rename control is later added.
- No free-text component-rename field exists: Commercial components currently have no free-text rename/label-edit field (see V-041). Should be re-verified on each catalogue refresh.
- No idempotency-key infrastructure exists anywhere in the product for a real external caller. The only idempotency protection today is each approve_*/submit_*/reject_*/send_back_*/save_* RPC's own internal status-guard/no-op-if-already-terminal logic, which only protects against a same-request-again scenario (double click, refresh-then-repeat, back/forward replay), not a distributed retry-with-idempotency-key scenario, since no external API write caller exists yet to need one (see all of Pack W).
- No cron/scheduled job exists anywhere in the codebase for Go Live/Entitlement or anything else observed in this catalogue's scope. Future-dated Go Live dates and monthly usage-vs-go-live-month gating are computed fresh on every read, never asynchronously (see X-009, Y-015, Z-019). Any future feature that assumes background/scheduled processing should be flagged against this current reality.
